LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset. … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20 Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 10 picks, including the Packers to spoil Kirk Cousins' return with the Vikings Imagn Images A perfect week. Can you believe it? I went 15-0 with my straight-up picks last week. I guess it was an easy week, like some said. As for my picks against the spread, it wasn't quite as good, but it was better than it's been. I went 9-6 for the week, which I will take. The season marks are now 59-74-3 ATS and 87-48-1 straight up. Let's see if we can get perfect against the spread this week. Yeah, right. I will take three games above. 500 again as I make the climb to respectability. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Giants are back home after beating the Eagles and now face a Commanders team that probably has to win this to have any chance at the playoffs. The Giants' defense has been dominant up front as of late, and that will continue here as they contain Jayden Daniels . Giants keep winning. Pick: Giants 23, Commanders 14 New England Patriots at Detroit Lions (-2.5) Munich on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams, but especially so for the Patriots after they got blown out by the Packers at home last week. The Lions won at Miami and didn't play great, but they will get it going on offense here. New England is struggling on defense, so look for the Lions to win it with a strong offensive showing. Pick: Lions 30, Patriots 24 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs snapped a two-game losing streak last week in beating the Jets , while the Falcons were blown out in Madrid by the Bengals . The defense had some major issues in that game. That will be the same here after the trade of safety Jessie Bates. Chiefs stack another victory. Pick: Chiefs 23, Falcons 17 Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns (+4.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns . But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. Pick: Texans 21, Browns 20 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) The Packers are coming off an impressive road victory over the Patriots and Jordan Love has been on fire. But the Minnesota defense is special and now they have Kirk Cousins to play quarterback. Even so, look for the Packers to win another one as their defense limits Cousins and the offense. Pick: Packers 27, Vikings 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-10.5) at Tennessee Titans The Titans are coming off a bye, while the Jaguars are coming off a victory last Thursday at Baltimore. They will be rested too. Jacksonville is riding high as one of the top teams in the league and made some moves at the trade deadline to get even better. Though this is a rivalry, with some unpredictable games, this won't be. Jaguars big. Pick: Jaguars 31, Titans 17 Miami Dolphins (+3.5) at Indianapolis Colts This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. Pick: Colts 23, Dolphins 22 Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints (-2.5) This is an enormous game in the division, even though both teams have just three victories. The winner will be in first place. The Saints beat the Browns last week, while the Panthers have lost three straight. The Saints make it four in a row as Tyler Shough has a big day. Pick: Saints 24, Panthers 21 Buffalo Bills (-8.5) at New York Jets The Bills are coming off a hard-fought road victory at Minnesota. The turnaround will be tough, but they are playing at a high level. The defense is improving. Look for Josh Allen to carve up the Jets' defense. Pick: Bills 34, Jets 21 Seattle Seahawks (-6.5) at Las Vegas Raiders Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Seahawks will start Drew Lock at quarterback again in this one. He was just OK last week against Arizona. But the Raiders have big-time defensive issues. For the Raiders, it's Fernando Mendoza time after they traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota. This is a tough defense for a first NFL start. Look for Lock to win it as the Seahawks' defense does the rest. Pick: Seahawks 24, Raiders 16 Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals (+9.5) The Rams lost at home to the Cardinals a few weeks ago and now must play without Puka Nacua . How will they move the ball? The Cardinals will start rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Going against Myles Garrett and company can be a problem. Rams win it, but it's low-scoring. Pick: Rams 19, Cardinals 16 San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys (+4.5) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys can't afford another loss in their division race, so this is a huge game for them. The 49ers are riding high and that offense will challenge the Dallas defense. But I think the Dallas offense will be even better. Upset special. Dak Prescott has a bigger day than Brock Purdy . Pick: Cowboys 30, 49ers 28 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is for first place in the division. The Bengals are riding high behind their passing game and Joe Burrow . But the defense can't stop the run. The Steelers will run it here to keep Burrow off the field. It doesn't work. The Bengals will once again win it behind Burrow and the passing game. It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Commanders, the full Week 10 slate The Giants and Commanders played to a draw five weeks ago. Who wll win this time? | Getty Images Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants and Washington Commanders kick off Week 10 of the NFL season Thursday night at what promises to be a rainy, chilly MetLife Stadium. Can the Giants solidify their NFC East lead, or will the race for the division title tighten? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the Week 10 matchups. Which version of the Giants will show up on Thursday night? Will we get the sloppy Giants that came out flat against the Philadelphia Eagles, or the tough, physical, and technically sound Giants that showed up against the Houston Texans? John Harbaugh's 9-1 record home record on Thursday Nights is encouraging. I would say that this is a game the Giants should win on paper, particularly with Washington missing some of their best players and their starting center in the concussion protocol. However, I'm also not convinced that these Giants can play a normal game and just take care of business. I keep waiting for the Giants to play a complete game and execute on offense and defense, but this team seems unable to be both consistent and explosive. I hope the offensive line comes prepared to bully an injured Washington defensive line and J.J. McCarthy isn't forced into low percentage throws every third down by long yardage situations. Likewise, I hope that Dennard Wilson comes out swinging on defense, but also has a counterpunch ready in case Jayden Daniels has an answer to the Cover-0 blitz. I'm picking the Giants here, but they can't afford to take Washington lightly or give Jayden Daniels the chance to catch his breath and swing the game. Tony Del Genio This is the Giants' second consecutive must-win game. You wouldn't think that when 5-2-1 plays 2-5-1, but (1) the Giants haven't beaten the Commanders since Jayden Daniels became their quarterback (even though Daniels didn't play in one of those losses), (2) despite their record, Washington has beaten the Seahawks and only narrowly lost to the 49ers and Rams while the Giants were beaten soundly by the Rams, the only good team they've faced, and still have the 49ers and Seahawks coming up, along with the Jaguars and Lions. A division loss greatly weakens their hold on the NFC East lead, their only real path to the playoffs. Terry McLaurin is out for the season, but in his place is Stefon Diggs, who did not face the Giants in the first game. Jacory Crosky-Merritt, who beat the Giants' run D for a 33-yard TD right off the bat in the first game, is also out. The Commanders are further decimated by injuries since their last meeting to key starters such as DT Daron Payne and IOL Lucas Patrick. So really the Giants should prevail. The problem is…containing the running of Daniels, which they did not do well in their first meeting (103 yards, by far his highest of the season, and his only 2 rushing TDs of the season). Hopefully Dennard Wilson will have a plan for that. If so, and if the Giants execute it, then the Giants can win. David Hartman The rematch of the NFL's only tie game of the season will be played in prime time on Thursday night, and for the ninth time in nine games, the Giants are playing a team that doesn't have a winning record. But you can throw the records out the window: The 5-2-1 Giants, at home, are just 1.5 point favorites over the 2-5-1 Commanders. Go figure… Big Blue won with defense and a strong kicking game on Sunday in Philadelphia, with Arvel Reese perhaps becoming a star in real time. It was an ugly win, with the offense producing just 19 points. The Giants will need more than that against Jayden Daniels and company on Thursday night. Cam Skattebo is expected back, and that's good news. New York couldn't run the ball on Sunday, which stagnated their offense. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) might miss this game, however, and the O-line struggled at Philadelphia as it was. J.J. McCarthy wasn't terrible on Sunday, but he wasn't especially good either and now he's dealing with a hip pointer. Jameis Winston led New York on its only touchdown drive while McCarthy was temporarily knocked from the game. McCarthy hasn't thrown a TD pass (or an interception) in either of his two starts. This figures to be a close game, just like the first one. It'll be fun to watch standout rookies Reese and Sonny Styles — college teammates at Ohio State last season — leading the way for each defense. Seriously – how did anyone score on the Buckeyes? Anyway, Dennard Wilson needs to find a way to keep Daniels from gashing his defense with his legs. He ran for 103 yards and two scores in the first game. This game could come down to intangibles like turnovers and special teams. The G-Men have been winning (or tying) close games and that's a reflection on good coaching to a degree, and favorable luck. In a game that should be close, who am I to pick against that? Pick: Giants in a squeaker Valentine's View We are not picking games by the spread here, but I am surprised the Giants are just 1.5-point favorites. That indicates a continuing lack of real belief in the Giants in the betting market. The Giants understand the opportunity they have in front of them, and how important this game is. In the rainy, windy, miserable conditions at MetLife Stadium Thursday evening I think you have to expect what has become a typical Giants game this season — close, somewhat sloppy, decided by who makes the plays and who properly handles the situations at the end of the game. I have far more faith in the Giants to do that than I do the Commanders. We all remember the Commanders stunning clock mismanagement at the end of the Week 5 tie with the Giants. That sort of questionable decision-making has continued to plague Washington, which is 1-3-1 in games decided by one score. If you could the Arizona game, which I do since it was decided on the game's final play, seven of the Giants eight games this season were one-score games. The Giants are 5-1-1 in those games. They have lived on the edge, and have shown an ability to survive. Is that formula sustainable forever? Maybe not. It does, though, make me feel good about the Giants' chances on Thursday. home.headline: Washington Commanders Rule Out 2 Players Ahead of Thursday’s Giants Game
home.blurb: Washington Commanders Rule Out 2 Players Ahead of Thursday's Giants Game Washington has ruled out two players. Starting center Lucas Patrick will miss the game with a concussion, while tight end Colson Yankoff will sit out with a knee injury. As for wide receiver Treylon Burks , whose status remained uncertain because of a foot injury that kept him out last week, he no longer carries an injury designation and will return to the Commanders' offense. Outside linebacker Malik Harrison is the only player still carrying an injury designation. He's questionable with a groin injury, and the Giants will likely determine his availability closer to kickoff. Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. The Washington Commanders are gearing up for arguably their biggest game of the season so far on Thursday night. They will travel to MetLife Stadium to take on the NFC East-leading Giants in a primetime matchup. The Commanders enter the game with a 2-5-1 record, while the Giants sit on the opposite end of the spectrum at 5-2-1. Both teams have a tie on their records after playing one another in a wild overtime finish a few weeks ago. Now, they meet for the final time this season, and if the Commanders want any chance of closing the gap in the division, this could very well be a must-win game. Both teams released their final injury reports on Wednesday. Although Washington has already dealt with a handful of season-ending injuries, the team has a fairly clean outlook heading into Thursday night. Neither player practiced at all this week, so these absences haven't caught Washington off guard. Nick Allegretti is expected to take over for Patrick at center. The final injury report for the New York Giants and the Washington Commanders ahead of their game at the Meadowlands on Thursday night. https://t.co/NO0AgGzk54 — Ralph Vacchiano (@RalphVacchiano) November 11, 2026 New York also has a relatively clean injury report heading into the prime-time showdown. Running back Cam Skattebo and quarterback J.J. McCarthy are both good to go after the Giants monitored their statuses throughout the week. home.headline: Commanders-Giants Final Injury Report: Lucas Patrick Out, Treylon Burks Expected Back Despite Missed Practice
home.blurb: Commanders-Giants Final Injury Report: Lucas Patrick Out, Treylon Burks Expected Back Despite Missed Practice Skip to main content SI.COM Lucas Patrick is out Thursday night against the New York Giants. The Commanders’ final injury report also ruled out tight end Colson Yankoff, leaving Washington to start Nick Allegretti at center in place of Patrick. Patrick entered concussion protocol during Sunday’s loss to the Rams, and rookie Matt Gulbin finished that game at center. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed Tuesday that Allegretti will start against New York. Gulbin got the call Sunday because he had been taking the center reps while Allegretti worked at guard, a decision I wrote more about earlier this week . According to Washington's official website, the Giants blitz at the third-highest rate in the NFL. Allegretti will have to help set the protection against that defense with Jayden Daniels behind him. Treylon Burks missed Wednesday’s practice with the foot injury that kept him out against the Rams, but he has no game designation. Quinn said the day off was planned after Burks got work Tuesday and that the receiver was expected to be ready Thursday. Washington did not practice Monday and held a walkthrough Tuesday, so those first two participation reports were estimates. Burks’ place on the active list will be confirmed with Thursday’s inactives. Yankoff did not practice during the short week because of a knee injury. His absence reaches beyond the tight end rotation: Washington credited him with 185 special teams snaps this season. John Bates (shoulder) was full all three days, and Chig Okonkwo (hip) was full Tuesday and Wednesday. Neither has a game designation. The Patriots, which are off to a 5-4 start, are coming off a 45-27 defeat at the hands of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers. Meanwhile, the Lions, which are sitting at 6-2, defeated the Miami Dolphins, 19-9, in their Week 9 tilt . New England – led by Mike Vrabel on the sidelines – has lost two of its last three games, including to the Chicago Bears in Week 7. Additionally, it sits basically in the middle of the pack in both points scored (23.4/game) and points allowed (23.0/g). Yet, the Patriots still possess a myriad of talent on both sides of the ball. On offense, they're led under center by third-year passer Drake Maye, who has thrown for 18 touchdowns, 2,282 yards and a league-high 11 interceptions through nine games. He's coming off a three-interception performance against the Packers in which he completed a season-low 55.3 percent of his passes. Maye's top target this year has been veteran tight end Hunter Henry, who has amassed 32 catches, 361 yards and two touchdowns through the season's first nine games. And on the ground, the Patriots are spearheaded by sixth-year back Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson, a fourth-round pick of New England, has accumulated 399 yards and two touchdowns, and is presently averaging 3.9 yards per carry. Then, on the defensive side of the ball, the Patriots have received strong performances this season from the likes of EDGE defenders Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder, cornerback Carlton Davis III and linebacker Christian Elliss. Ponder, a second-year pro , has already recorded 7.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss and 13 QB hits, and has returned a fumble for a touchdown. And for his efforts, he's earned a 75.0 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, the 23rd-best overall grade among 110 qualified players at the position. The Patriots will not, however, have the services of Davis (knee) for this Week 10 international affair. Plus, they will also be down starting left guard Ben Brown (knee), and are expected to be without Stevenson (knee). Stevenson, the team's No. 1 back, suffered a plantaris tendon tear last week against the Packers. Those are three significant losses for Vrabel's squad going into its matchup with Detroit. As for the Lions, they will also be down multiple starters in Week 10: linebacker Jack Campbell (neck), center Cade Mays (ankle) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip). Plus, safety Kerby Joseph, who has yet to play a single game in 2026, will not be making his season debut in Germany. While both teams are rather significantly banged up, I still believe this matchup favors Detroit. At this present juncture, I believe the Lions have a 59 percent chance to secure their fifth straight victory. The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It's been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it'll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots' 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers' worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: "Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven't turned the ball over, they haven't exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it's just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven't quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error." The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

Injuries and inconsistencies are a big reason for that, but so is the drop-off in play from Drake Maye. He has already set a career-high in interceptions with 11, giving New England fans a legitimate reason to be concerned. Regardless of the situation around him, the Patriots have no chance if their quarterback can't turn it around. 3. The great outdoors: It's no secret that Jared Goff has trouble playing football when there is no roof above him. He is 1-2 in outdoor games this season, most recently defeating the Dolphins . However, Detroit's offense struggled to score points in Miami, resurfacing the questions about Goff's struggles when dealing with the elements. In fairness to Goff, he had a stellar game against the Bills earlier this season, though that did come with more ideal weather conditions. Unfortunately for the Lions, they are back outside this week in Germany and the forecast isn't as comfortable, with calls for temperatures in the 40s and 50s. Will Campbell and Ben Brown both hurt their knees against Green Bay, A.J. Brown has missed two straight, and the backfield has its own injury questions with Corey Kiner in line for RB1 reps. Maye can still make enough plays to keep this interesting, especially if he gets some help back. But the Lions can put the Patriots in a bind with Jahmyr Gibbs on the ground and Jared Goff off play-action. It's hard not to trust the Lions to finish more drives after what we just watched in Foxborough. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Lions 30, Patriots 28 New England heads to Munich trying to leave its various problems stateside. Drake Maye could be in for a bounce-back performance if he can show more restraint with unforced errors. away.headline: A big Munich test for Lions and Patriots as injuries loom for New England
away.blurb: Injuries are a top concern for New England. Before traveling Wednesday night, the Patriots ruled out LG Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness). November 12, 2026 / 5:07 PM EST / AP Heading into international games, NFL coaches typically talk up the niceties of "growing the game" globally. The New England Patriots (5-4) have lost two of their past three games and have a slew of injury concerns, including running back Rhamondre Stevenson. The Detroit Lions, even with a 6-2 record and four straight victories, are trying to keep pace in the tight NFC North. Sunday's game in Munich is a big one for both teams. Lions coach Dan Campbell wasn't focused on the international implications. "Well, if I'm being honest, I just haven't thought that far into it. I'm like, 'We've got to get prepared,'" Campbell said. The Patriots were embarrassed at home by the Green Bay Packers last week, losing 45-27, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions and the secondary struggling to contain the Packers' passing game. Campbell expects a much-improved New England team on Sunday. "You look at the totality of what this team is capable of, the firepower they have, and they're a good team. They're dangerous," he said. "And they're going to clean a lot of things up." The Lions slogged through a 19-9 win over the rebuilding Miami Dolphins last week, relying on four field goals from Jake Bates. It was also just one week after a neck injury to All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell. Detroit's bye week is in the rearview mirror, and after Munich, the team will host Tampa Bay and then Chicago on Thanksgiving Day. "It's a good thing to be tested during the season," Campbell said. "It really is. And to have to go through some of these tough stretches because that's what the playoffs are. That's what it is. And certainly if you got to go on the road. So, that's what this is. This is about us. This is the next obstacle we have. Told the team we're not going to clear it. Our objective is to go through it, and that's the mindset." Stevenson, the team's leading rusher with 399 yards on 102 carries, didn't practice Wednesday because of a knee injury. That could put second-year running back Corey Kiner in line for the bulk of the carries. "Corey has done a really nice job, but there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on," coach Mike Vrabel said, citing "recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure." The coach said "a lot of contending teams" are 5-4. "We've got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January," Vrabel said. "It's usually what happens in the National Football League; a bunch of teams get bunched up, and they go in different directions, and I know the direction that we're going to head in, and that's going to be the one that's forward, positive and winning." New England (5-4) vs. Detroit (6-2) in Munich, Germany. When/where to watch: S

home.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? Ahead of their game on Sunday against the Patriots, Goff landed on the injury report at Wednesday's practice. Lions Announce Jared Goff Injury Update Ahead of Patriots Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL It's official: Poch to Man United Lions Announce Jared Goff Injury Update Ahead of Patriots Game Gavin Groe · Athlon Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 9:39 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Detroit Lions are rolling, winners of four straight games heading into their international matchup in Germany against the New England Patriots. While the defense has stepped up over the past month, the offensive unit led by quarterback Jared Goff has been incredible all season long. Goff has thrown for 2,134 yards across eight games, completing 67.8% of his pass attempts. He has thrown 15 total touchdowns and just two interceptions, taking good care of the football. The Lions have been one of the league's best offenses and while offensive coordinator Drew Petzing deserves some credit, it starts with Goff's ability to operate under pressure. Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16)USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect He does take some hits while he stays in the pocket and it is unclear if the injury originated last Sunday during the team's win over the Miami Dolphins, but it was enough to limit Goff and add some concern. However, all the doubts about Goff suiting up can be officially put to rest. Just one day later, the Lions announced Goff was a full participant at Thursday's practice, signaling that he will be under center on Sunday unless he suffers a setback. The Lions are going to need Goff to perform well again in Week 9 against a tough New England defense, and to also ensure they do what they can to make the NFL playoffs. The NFC is a tough conference this year and even at 6-2, the Lions are second in the NFC North behind the Chicago Bears. Related: NFL Facing Punishment Decision After Jared Goff Play

Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Joshua Schulman · Kansas City Chiefs On SI Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After making a statement at Arrowhead Stadium, the Kansas City Chiefs will head back out on the road in Week 10 as the hosting Atlanta Falcons will attempt to play spoiler. KC is looking to build on its blowout win over the Jets in its previous outing. The Falcons have lost four of their past five matchups but aren't technically out of it given the dire state of the NFC South. As a result, Kevin Stefanski's group is viewing this contest as a must-win if they want to stay in the playoff race. Despite Kansas City's impressive 6-2 record, Andy Reid and Co. have dealt with special teams struggles and offensive inconsistencies. Those issues have put a damper on what has otherwise been a successful start. Most analysts view the Chiefs as heavy favorites, but what does the ESPN Matchup Predictor forecast? Here's what the computer model expects two days before kickoff. Chiefs at Falcons: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction Sep 22, 2024; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Darnell Mooney (1) is hit after making a catch against the Kansas City Chiefs during the second half at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 78.1%, Falcons 21.6%. With nearly a four-in-five chance of coming out victorious, the matchup predictor heavily favors Kansas City this weekend. Chiefs on SI's Take Chiefs fans can only take things one week at a time. Until the Broncos lose and give Kansas City an opening, all the Chiefs can do is beat the opponents in front of them. The biggest storyline of this road clash is the arrival of Josh Downs , who landed with the Chiefs shortly before the trade deadline passed. The shifty slot receiver may not be featured too much out of the gate due to his unfamiliarity with the playbook, but there are bound to be some bright spots in his debut in the red and gold. Kenneth Walker III is a dynamic weapon in the backfield , but Bijan Robinson is on another level. In spite of poor quarterback play, Robinson is virtually unstoppable in the open field and possesses elite vision as a runner. He has three games in which he surpassed 100 yards this season and is averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Atlanta is unsurprisingly a significant underdog coming into this one, though it really depends on which version of the Falcons show up on Sunday. They were blown out by the Bengals last time out and shut out by the Buccaneers a week prior, but they also hold upset victories over the 49ers and Packers. The drastic shifts in Atlanta's play have fans scratching their heads, largely due to the play of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. A week after taking home NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors in Week 7, he tossed a career-high four interceptions and failed to get his team a point. Heading into their final game before a bye, the Falcons are going to throw everything they can at the visiting squad to stay in contention. This is the type of matchup that could see the Chiefs fall into an early deficit if they aren't careful. Kansas City is coming off a convincing 35-12 win over the New York Jets, a game that turned after the Chiefs trailed 12-7 in the second quarter. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both scoring passes going to Kenneth Walker III , who was the offensive centerpiece with 102 rushing yards, 143 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Travis Kelce added 72 receiving yards and even scored on a one-yard run. The defense took over after halftime, holding New York scoreless in the final thirty minutes as the Chiefs pulled away with 21 unanswered second-half points. Kansas City also went 4-for-4 in the red zone, an encouraging development after back-to-back losses to Seattle and Denver. Mahomes did briefly leave the field after hurting his arm/elbow on a strip-sack but returned and finished the game. As a result, the injury report is worth following as gametime approaches. Atlanta, meanwhile, returns home after a disappointing 34-17 loss to Cincinnati in Madrid, its second straight defeat following a 16-0 shutout loss at Tampa Bay. The Falcons opened strongly against the Bengals with an 80-yard drive resulting in a Michael Penix Jr. touchdown pass to Charlie Woerner . The scoring continued as they took a 10-7 lead later in the first quarter, but Cincinnati answered with 17 unanswered points in the second quarter and Atlanta never recovered. Penix finished 20-of-31 for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Bijan Robinson supplied the offense’s biggest bright spot with 100 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Drake London caught five passes for 68 yards, but Atlanta committed 12 penalties for 88 yards and allowed Joe Burrow to throw three touchdown passes. The central storyline from Atlanta’s perspective is will they be able to control the ball and keep Mahomes and co. off the field? The Falcons average 138.8 yards rushing per game. For Kansas City, it is about limiting Bijan Robinson and Atlanta’s rushing attack. The Chiefs have thrived against the run to date this season allowing just 96.3 yards on the ground per game. These teams last met two seasons ago. Mercedes-Benz Stadium was the site and Kansas City won 22-17. Mahomes threw for 217 yards and two touchdowns, while Rashee Rice caught 12 passes for 110 yards and a score; Atlanta, then quarterbacked by Kirk Cousins , had a chance late but could not complete the comeback. picks.headline: Chiefs-Falcons betting line & prediction: Will Josh Downs make instant impact?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. The Chiefs acquired receiver Josh Downs, who is expected to debut Sunday in Atlanta. Patrick Mahomes practiced fully Wednesday after an elbow injury scare vs. Jets. The betting line lists Kansas City as a 3.5-point favorite over Atlanta. The Kansas City Chiefs stopped a two-game losing streak Sunday with their 35-12 win over the New York Jets to improve to 6-2. Earlier Sunday, the Atlanta Falcons lost their second straight game, falling 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals at Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. The loss dropped Atlanta to 3-6. How to watch Chiefs at Falcons Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -3.5 Behind the KC-ATL matchup The Chiefs and Falcons look a little different than they did last week, before the NFL’s trade deadline. Kansas City made the highly anticipated move Tuesday to acquire wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . Meanwhile, Atlanta began the week by agreeing to trade three-time second-team All-Pro safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars before sending starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens. Downs is expected to make his Chiefs debut Sunday in Atlanta. He recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown for the Colts this season. Downs’ stat line included seven catches for 72 yards against Kansas City in Week 2. “I had to watch him live. Yeah, which wasn’t good,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, drawing laughter from reporters. To earn extended playing time Sunday, Downs will have to demonstrate that he can handle Reid’s complex playbook. Kansas City kept that in mind while shopping for receivers. “That’s what we felt about Josh — that he has that ability,” Reid said. “And now it’s just a matter of him spending the time to knock it out. But he’s a pretty alert kid.” How Downs fits alongside Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy will be worth watching, but the good news for the Chiefs is that his debut should come with Patrick Mahomes under center. Mahomes suffered an injury scare late in the second quarter against the Jets. Mahomes hurt his elbow but remained in the game, and medical test results were encouraging. He was listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. In an encouraging development, Worthy (hamstring) also participated fully. “I feel like I’m in a great spot,” Mahomes said. “Now it’s just about pain and pain management and stuff like that, which I’ll try to do whatever I can to be in the best place possible.” While much of the focus will be on Downs’ Chiefs debut and how Mahomes attacks a Falcons secondary playing its first game without Bates, the path to victory is likely to look familiar. Running back Kenneth Walker presents a favorable matchup against an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 yards per carry. After two less productive games by his lofty standards, Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards against the Jets , adding four receptions for 41 yards and three total touchdowns. Following his breakout performance in Denver, rookie Emmett Johnson rushed for 34 yards and a touchdown on six carries against New York. Asked about the Falcons’ defense, Reid highlighted edge rusher James Pearce, who returned last week for 15 snaps after serving an eight-game suspension to begin the season. The former first-round pick registered 10.5 sacks as a rookie in 2025. Pearce (back) missed practice Wednesday, so his status is worth monitoring. “(The Falcons are) fast — and even faster when they’re on their turf,” Reid said. “So they’re very athletic. They’ve got some young linebackers that are flying around. They’ve got that front, and they rotate those guys.” With right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) out of practice Wednesday, Josh Ezeudu could be in line to make his second start of the season. Pearce can line up on either side of the line, and he will be a challenge for both Ezeudu and Chiefs left tackle Kahlil Benson. The Falcons feature 11 players with at least one sack, including defensive end Za’Darius Smith (4.5), defensive end Cameron Thomas (2) and defensive tackle LaCale London (2) — all with at least two sacks on the season. On offense, the Falcons’ biggest threat is running back Bijan Robinson, the only player in the league with more rushing yards (880) than Walker (872), though with one additional game. “He’s electricity in a bottle,” Chiefs linebacker Nick Bolton said of Robinson. “That’s what I say. (He’s) able to change direction, get upfield, cutbacks. We see all the time everybody’s at the point of attack because he can cut it back and put pressure on the back-side corner on the outside zone to the opposite side. So he’s electricity in a bottle, like I said, and it’ll take all hands on deck.” Much like Kansas City, Atlanta wants its running game to create opportunities through the air. Robinson’s presence helps open things up for quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and wide receiver Drake London, who leads the Falcons with 692 receiving yards but only one touchdown. The Chiefs listed cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) as a full participant Wednesday, and his return after a two-game absence would help Kansas City match up against London. Kansas City’s defensive front will look to build on its momentum after sacking Jets quarterback Geno Smith five times last Sunday. Defensive end George Karlaftis and defensive tackle Chris Jones recorded two sacks apiece. According to NFL NextGen Stats, Penix posts a league-worst 34% completion percentage when under pressure. Jones should have an advantage over center Corey Levin, who is expected to make his first start of the season after replacing Neuzil. A sixth-round pick in 2017, Levin has spent most of his career in a reserve role. Despite kicker Harrison Butker’s recent struggles, Reid announced Wednesday that he would stick with him for now, with Justin Tucker waiting on the practice squad. Perhaps a homecoming for Butker, an Atlanta native, sparks the turnaround he’s been seeking. Chiefs-Falcons game prediction As evidenced by their respective deadline moves, the Chiefs are all in on 2026, as the Falcons look toward the future. Kansas City draws energy from Downs’ debut, Delane helps neutralize London and the pass rush builds on last week’s solid outing. Winner: Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 | Cover: Chiefs Sweeney’s record: (6-2-0) | Against the spread: (4-4-0) This story was originally published November 12, 2026 at 7:00 AM . Bleacher Report's Moe Moton believes Tyreek Hill could return as a bargain signing for Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City also reportedly called the New York Jets about Garrett Wilson and was turned away. Hill is still recovering from a major knee injury, and a civil jury found him liable on two battery charges. His agent says medical clearance is close, though he gave no date. The Chiefs still have time to add more help for Mahomes. Tyreek Hill reunion could still make sense for the Chiefs Moton did not hide the risks. Hill's knee is a real question after last season, and the civil verdict will shape how teams see him. “Hill's injury recovery and the civil jury's findings could factor into teams' evaluations, though a team willing to sign him may still see potential for the explosiveness that made him a game-changing receiver,” Moton wrote. He does not expect Hill back before Thanksgiving. For Kansas City, that timing works. The Chiefs would add a receiver for the final stretch instead of waiting through a long rehab, and Hill already spent six seasons in this offense. “Even with the addition of wideout Josh Downs, the Chiefs may consider reuniting with Hill to add another playmaker for Patrick Mahomes,” Moton wrote. home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 10's game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Chiefs have quite a few injuries to consider heading into Week 10, but it's not nearly as bad as it could be. In fact, there are a few pleasant surprises. Both Patrick Mahomes and Xavier Worthy fully participated in practice on Wednesday . Worthy, in particular, feels like a blessing. He had a non-contact hamstring injury late in the fourth quarter of Week 9 vs. the Jets. Another pleasant surprise? A few more players are full participants after being limited in recent weeks. Here’s a quick breakdown of each team’s Week 10 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Nov. 13. It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Texans vs. Browns Week 10 picks: Cleveland being treated like an afterthought Chris Pokorny · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:37 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cleveland Browns take on the Houston Texans this Sunday. The Browns are 3-0 at home this year, but after having lost two straight games, they are being treated like an afterthought this week. As you can see in the national picks below, not a single person is picking the Browns at home. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 10 game between the Browns and Texans: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Texans: Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy. The real key to that success is Nico Collins. In the 257 snaps Collins has played this season, the Texans have averaged 8.2 yards per passing play, more than the 49ers' league-leading 7.9. He could be stalled when matched up against cornerback Denzel Ward, who's allowing 0.5 yards per coverage snap, fifth-fewest among cornerbacks (min. 150 coverage snaps). That duel is sure to be dogfight Sunday, but no matter, as I have faith in Stroud's other weapons (Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr., Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson) to get it done. Houston's lone offensive weakness matches up nicely against the Browns' permeable run defense. Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team. Thus, Cleveland will fall short of improving to 4-0 at home for the first time since the 1963 campaign, when Jim Brown led the NFL in rushing and scrimmage yards in a 14-game season. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Texans 21, Browns 20 This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns. But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. CBS Sports (John Breech) – Texans 24, Browns 16 Anyway, this genuinely does feel like a game that's going to boil down to Watson vs. the Texans. Watson has been sacked more times than any other QB in the NFL this year (33), and he'll be facing a defense that leads the NFL in sacks (29). That's a recipe for disaster. There have only been three games all season where a QB has been sacked at least eight times: Two of them were Deshaun Watson (vs. Jets in Week 5 and vs. Steelers in Week 8) and the other one happened on Sunday with the Texans sacking Justin Herbert eight times. Sporting News (Vinnie Iyer) – Texans 20, Browns 17 The Texans hope to sneak back into the playoff picture and their defense got back to making big plays in Los Angeles after the bye. Cleveland's defense will get a break as Houston is one-dimensional out of necessity, but in the end, old Texans friend Deshaun Watson will be outdueled by red-hot C.J. Stroud. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Texans 22, Browns 19 Shedeur Sanders had 297 passing yards and two TDs in his first start of the season, and that might be enough to keep that in a home start against the Texans. Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud is coming off a 384-yard, five-TD performance against the Chargers. The Browns' early-season shine is wearing off, but they are 4-0 ATS as an underdog of seven points or less. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger, who has 25 tackles the last two weeks, helps Cleveland stick around at home. Below are our Week 10 NFL staff picks:

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Houston Texans (3-5) head to Cleveland on Sunday looking to continue a dramatic midseason turnaround when they face the Browns (5-4) at Huntington Bank Field. The Texans opened the season with four straight losses but have won three of their last four. The division may be out of reach as the Jaguars lead the Texans by three games in the AFC South but Houston is back in the race for a Wild Card spot. Cleveland takes the field after dropping their last two games which has dropped them out of first in the AFC North and 1.5 games behind the Steelers and the Bengals. Houston is coming off its most explosive performance of the season, a 44-22 road rout of the winless Los Angeles Chargers. C.J. Stroud played through an illness and completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. He connected with four different players for scores, including 63-yard touchdowns to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte , with Boutte finishing with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The Texans led 24-9 at halftime, stretched the advantage to 38-9 early in the fourth quarter and defensively overwhelmed Justin Herbert , sacking him eight times. Cleveland arrives home following a gut-wrenching 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. With Deshaun Watson sidelined by a concussion, Shedeur Sanders started and finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 64-yard go-ahead strike to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter. After New Orleans regained the lead, Andre Szmyt’s 51-yard field goal forced overtime. The Saints scored first in the extra period, but Sanders answered by finding Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown before Cleveland went for two and the win; the conversion failed, dropping the Browns to 5-4. The matchup also renews a surprisingly balanced series. Houston leads the all-time matchup 8-7, including the postseason, but Cleveland won four consecutive meetings from 2020 through the 2023 regular season. Their most recent clash reversed that trend in emphatic fashion: in the 2023 AFC Wild Card round, Stroud threw for 274 yards and three touchdowns as Houston demolished Cleveland 45-14, with the Texans turning two Joe Flacco interceptions into defensive touchdowns. In addition to Watson’s health, other storylines include the Texans’ pass rush against Cleveland’s quarterback protection particularly after Sanders was sacked five times in New Orleans and Houston just recorded eight sacks against the Chargers. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Texans' Injury Report Raises Concerns on Woody Marks, Marvin Harrison Jr.
away.blurb: Something that immediately sticks out from the Texans' Thursday injury report that wasn't present on their previous one: both Marks and Harrison Jr. were DNP in practice with their respective issues. In the event both were to miss out on Sunday, the Texans would be down to just two players in their running back room: veteran Dare Ogunbowale and recently-signed Emari Demercado. In Harrison Jr.'s case, he also has yet to miss a game for the Texans this season since his arrival. His only missed game of the season came back in Week 5 when he was with the Arizona Cardinals and was left to sit out knowing that a trade to send him out to Houston was imminent . Another injury to keep an eye on for someone who still practiced in limited capacity? Defensive end Danielle Hunter, who was not listed on the injury report on Wednesday, yet popped up as a late entry on Thursday with a hamstring issue. The Houston Texans have released their second of three injury reports of the week heading into their upcoming matchup against the Cleveland Browns. And for one of the few times this season, the Texans' Thursday injury report happened to showcase a few more concerns from what was shown on the first day of practice –– particularly in the case of two key offensive pieces: running back Woody Marks and wide receiver Marvin Harrison. Let's take a look at the latest on the Texans' injury report only a few days away from Week 10's matchup Houston Texans Injury Report (as of 11/12) LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin/personal) OL Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder) S Reed Blankenship (hand/concussion) It'd be a noteworthy, but also rare absence for both players in the event they were set to miss this weekend's action in Cleveland. Marks (knee) has been active in every game for the Texans so far this season. Throughout the past three weeks since David Montgomery has been sidelined with his groin issue, Marks has been the leader in Houston's backfield, claiming a lion's share of the offensive reps. During last week's game against the LA Chargers , Marks put together 18 carries for 70 yards (3.9 yards per carry), making it his fourth-straight game logging over 70 all-purpose yards. If he were to miss any time at all for Week 10, his absence could wind up being significant for a Texans backfield that's been stuck without Montgomery, and could continue to be against the Browns, depending on how his status shifts heading into the weekend. His absence––if he were to miss this week with a hamstring ailment––would slim the Texans' receiver room down once more, considering they just had to deal with the loss of Jaylin Noel after Week 7 against the New York Giants . That means more involvement for Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Xavier Hutchinson, and Kayshon Boutte, and especially so if the Texans' backfield is without its top two contributors in Marks and Montgomery. away.headline: Texans Injury Report vs. Browns Week 10: Multiple Starters Miss Practice
away.blurb: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans made it known that Montgomery's status has improved from last week ––when he was ruled out with a groin injury on Wednesday––but said he would continue to be evaluated throughout the week. It remains to be seen if he ends up playing once the weekend rolls around. Azeez Al-Shaair might be a name to keep an eye on, as he was a DNP with seemingly the same groin injury that's restricted his availability in practice as of late . However, given that he also had a personal designation, there's a better chance that he'll be good to go for either Thursday or Friday's session. Tight end Brevin Jordan also wound up as a DNP in practice with a finger/foot issue. If he's unable to go against the Browns, Houston has four other tight ends on the roster to turn to instead, including second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who was active on the gameday against the LA Chargers for the first time since Week 4. The Texans' final status for everyone on the roster will become clearer after Friday's practice. But until then, keep a close watch on those four who didn't practice, while also not losing sight of anyone who was limited for Wednesday’s action. Texans Final Injury Report for Week 9 vs. Chargers: Who's In, Who's Out The Houston Texans have wrapped up their first day of practice ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. And following that practice session for the Texans, we've gotten a glimpse of the injuries that this roster is dealing with in the days ahead of this weekend's contest––where in Houston's case, there's a chance that they could be forced to play without one or more of their typical starters. Let's break down the latest from the Texans' Wednesday injury report before facing the Browns in Week 10. Houston Texans Injury Report (as of 11/11) LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin/personal) OG Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder) S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) DT Tommy Togiai (elbow/shoulder) The most notable takeaways from the Texans' first injury report of the week surround the four names who were listed as DNPs; three of them being starters. David Montgomery is the least surprising of the four, who has missed each of the Texans' team practices since leaving Week 5's game against the Tennessee Titans with a groin injury, and has gradually been working his way back to the lineup. The Texans also ended up seeing rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge pop up as a rare entry on the injury report, as Coach Ryan’s noted that he had suffered a stinger during practice and would be listed as day-to-day. The stinger doesn't initially seem like something that would inhibit Rutledge's status for Sunday, but he'll have two more practices to go in order to see whether or not he'll be able to suit up. If Rutledge is indeed sidelined for whatever reason this weekend, veteran Wyatt Teller could be the primary name to look towards as Houston's next man up at left guard. He's started two games already this season in place of Ed Ingram

home.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
home.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury | Sporting News Skip to main content SN 140 Horse Racing Horse Racing Latest News More Sports More Sports Latest News Fantasy Fantasy See More Football News Betting Betting See More Explore Betting Home Predictions Prediction Markets See More Explore Predictions Home Watch Watch How to Watch US Streaming Services Apple TV Patrick Gorski/Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns are heading into their Week 9 matchup with a 5-3 record, looking to keep pace with the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers in the AFC North. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9. He will go up against a very leaky Saints defense that has allowed plenty of teams to put up very big offensive days. MORE : Joe Burrow joins rare NFL history with six touchdowns despite three interceptions With Harold Fannin Jr., Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson, Denzel Boston, and KC Concepcion, Sanders has a much better supporting cast this season than he did for much of last year. Sanders is the Browns' Week 9 starter against the Saints, which will be his first real chance to play in his second NFL season after a Pro Bowl rookie year. home.headline: Texans’ Will Anderson Jr. pops up on injury report before Browns game
home.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? Anderson was listed as a limited participant in practice after not appearing on Wednesday's report, according to the injury report shared by Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com. It is unclear when the ankle injury occurred. Houston will be hoping to have its defensive leader available as it looks to build on a 44-22 blowout win over the Los Angeles Chargers last week. The Texans are 3-5 on the season, but they have won three of their last four games. Anderson is not the only Texans pass rusher on the injury report. Danielle Hunter was also added on Thursday with a hamstring injury and was limited in practice. Houston also has some concerns on offense. Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. was downgraded to a non-participant with a hamstring injury, while running back Woody Marks did not practice due to a knee issue.
