LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Commanders +2.5): The last time these two teams faced off, they TIED. I'm expecting another close game and may be leaning toward the underdog. Washington played the Los Angeles Rams tough last Sunday and held Matthew Stafford and Co. to 20 points. J.J. McCarthy has looked solid with his new team, but he actually just became the only quarterback in the past 40 seasons to register a win with zero passing touchdowns in four straight starts (dating back to last year). He suffered a hip injury vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , while Cam Skattebo is coming off a hamstring strain. Both will play, but I do wonder how much those issues could linger. The Commanders are 4-0-1 straight up and 4-1 against the spread (ATS) in their last five against the New York Giants , so I'll take the points here in a potential upset. … Prediction: Commanders 21, Giants 20 Dubin (Giants -2.5): I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith that this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. … Prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 14 New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Now, the two teams will conclude their regular-season series with a chilly match at Lambeau Field. Vikings fans are still riding the excitement from a major adrenaline injection early this week as the team reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins via trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. What once looked like a potential beatdown in Green Bay now looks like a massive opportunity for the Vikings to end a two-game losing streak and sweep their biggest rival. There’s still a lot up in the air, especially since head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn't technically named Cousins the starter yet. But let’s be real: Cousins is starting unless there's a major setback . So, let’s dive into some predictions for Sunday, assuming “Kirko Chainz” makes his triumphant return. 1. Justin Jefferson returns to form (for real this time) Frick it, Justin Jefferson is down there somewhere. There is perhaps no larger beneficiary of the Cousins’ reunion tour than Jefferson. The seventh-year wide receiver is on pace to have the worst year of his career after poor QB play wrecked his 2025 campaign. Needless to say, it’s time for Jefferson to reclaim his spot on the wide receiver throne. Jefferson’s 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins far surpasses his 65 ypg average through six full games this season. Cousins’ mission on Sunday is simple: feed Jefferson. I’m predicting Jefferson will have a vintage performance with over 150 receiving yards and at least one touchdown. #Vikings QB Kirk Cousins says he saw Justin Jefferson today, and is excited to play with him again: “You don’t go chasing things, but you understand the player he is, and you go where your reads take you. You know he tends to make it right when you throw in his direction.” pic.twitter.com/zOoSnvilDO 2. Vikings defense holds the Packers to less than 20 points Green Bay’s 24 points per game ranks 12th-highest in the league through nine weeks, while Brian Flores and the Vikings defense are allowing a league-low 14.5 points per game to opposing offenses. Minnesota has held two of the league's best offenses, Detroit and Buffalo, to 19 and 23 points, respectively. This feat is even more impressive given the complete lack of help on the offensive side of the ball. “This roster has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing.” -Vikings GM Nolan Teasley on the decision to trade for Kirk Cousins pic.twitter.com/TkkJVs0fsp 3. Minnesota gets back in the win column This one is pretty straightforward: I have the Vikings righting the ship against a talented Packers team and ending their slide down the NFC North standings. While many had assumed star pass rusher Micah Parsons would be back by now, the Vikings have the distinct advantage of avoiding him in both regular-season matchups. Two of these teams will miss the playoffs pic.twitter.com/7VewNM4oiT With a reenergized offense, a motivated Cousins returning to the scene of a career-altering injury, and O’Connell in “prove it” mode, I think we finally see a well-rounded 2026 Vikings squad in action. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christopher Gates · SB Nation Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:13 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division's basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don't like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday's game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that's just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don't do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they'll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We'll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it'll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they've been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, November 12, 2026 at 1:48 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It wasn't that long ago that Kirk Cousins, in his first stint with the Minnesota Vikings, was the quarterback who could never win the big one . Everyone remembers this critique of him. These days, Kirk Cousins is 38. And somehow, everyone spent days and weeks arguing that the only way for the Vikings to have a chance to win the big one was to trade for Cousins. That trade did happen, and it was perfectly reasonable for the Vikings to see if Cousins can guide them to an NFC North title and maybe a playoff run. They have the defense for it but we saw on Monday night that the offense was beyond repair with the quarterback situation they had. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was hesitant to announce Cousins would start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, but the Vikings didn't trade for Cousins to watch Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz start in a huge divisional game. While the trade for Cousins was reasonable, the Vikings still have the fourth-best quarterback in the division and the fourth-best offense in the division as well. Cousins is an upgrade but mostly because the Vikings had a dreadful quarterback situation. The Packers didn't do anything at the trade deadline but it might be because they've been on quite a roll. They were not good through three weeks but somehow have emerged as one of the better teams in the NFL since then. Since Week 4, they're fourth in EPA ( expected points added ) per play on offense and third in EPA per play allowed on defense. It's a good team. Anyone will have issues with the Vikings' defense and we'll see if the Packers' deep passing game can function against Minnesota's many blitzes. But Packers -3 is the pick. Taking the Vikings and Cousins, five days after rejoining the team, against a red-hot team is too much to ask. New Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) shown facing the Packers in a 2023 game. Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 10 of the NFL season: Commanders (+2.5) over Giants The Giants are three games up on the Commanders in the NFC East, but New York isn't that great. The Commanders come in as the more desperate team. Their season is all but over if they lose on Thursday. That's not the best reason to pick a team, but it's good enough in a game between two flawed teams. Patriots (+2.5) over Lions This is the NFL's last early-morning game of the season. The Lions and Patriots meet in Germany. The Patriots are coming off a bad loss to the Packers, and have their running back issues with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson out. One factor to consider is the Lions aren't the same team outdoors. Jared Goff's rating in domes is 102.9 and outdoors it is 92.4. There is some noise in those numbers, and Goff's ratings haven't had that big of a gap the past two seasons, but Detroit also just scored 19 points at Miami last week. That and the Lions' defensive deficiencies are enough to take the Patriots and the points. Texans (-4.5) over Browns The Browns have a better record, but also a -35 point differential. It's not like the Texans have been great, but there's a path for them to make the playoffs. They also know they can't drop games like this one. C.J. Stroud is playing well enough that points shouldn't be too hard for Houston to come by. Titans (+10.5) over Jaguars The Jaguars have taken over as my Super Bowl pick after the deadline. However, 10.5 is a lot of points in the NFL and the Titans have played three close games in a row. They're coming off their bye and have some extra rest. The Jaguars can't blow everyone out, right? Colts (-3.5) over Dolphins It's very hard to take the Colts, especially because the Dolphins are playing hard. The Colts played hard last week, but have to be deflated after losing that game to the Cowboys in the final minutes and seeing more players traded away. But it's even harder to back new Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord, a 2025 sixth-round pick who has never taken an NFL snap, playing with a subpar group. McCord gets the start for Miami with Malik Willis on injured reserve. Jets (+8) over Bills Talk about an ugly NFL side to take. The Jets are not good. But the Bills are coming off a physical game in Minnesota on Monday night and now go on the road to face the Jets on short rest. It seems unwise to take the Jets, but point spreads exist for a reason. Panthers (+2.5) over Saints The Saints are probably better in theory than reality. They won last week, but needed to defend a two-point conversion in overtime to knock off Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. It feels like the Saints have the potential to be the best team in the NFC South, but there's not much evidence they are. The Panthers are in a slump but have been the better team. Chiefs (-3.5) over Falcons It's not like the Falcons trading Jessie Bates III makes them significantly worse, but it's a difficult message for the locker room. It makes it seem like the front office is waving the white flag. In reality they got an offer they couldn't turn down, but it's still worth wondering how the remaining players will react. And Kansas City is a pretty good team. Cardinals (+9.5) over Rams For the rest of the season, or at least until Puka Nacua or Davante Adams returns, the Rams will try to survive by running the ball and playing defense in low-scoring games. There's not much explosiveness in the offense without any dangerous receivers. That will make them tough to back when the spread is large. Can Carson Beck lead the Arizona offense to enough points against a good Rams defense to cover any spread? That's the key question. Seahawks (-6.5) over Raiders This isn't a pick due to Fernando Mendoza facing the Seahawks defense, though that is a factor. It's because the Raiders defense is horrible. Since Week 3, after the Raiders had faced the offensively challenged Dolphins and Chargers, they're last in the NFL in EPA by a wide margin. They're 32nd in yards allowed and points allowed. The Seahawks will be able to move the ball, even with Drew Lock at quarterback. 49ers (-4.5) over Cowboys There are no signs the Cowboys are ready to have some kind of breakout. Last week they almost lost to a Colts team that has already given up on the season. And now they're supposed to keep it close against the 49ers, who have arguably been the best team in the NFL? Steelers (+3.5) over Bengals The Joe Burrow-for-MVP bandwagon is still running , but it's hard to lay more than a field goal in what should be a great divisional game. The Steelers can run the ball, and run defense is a weakness of the Bengals. They're last in the NFL in yards allowed per carry. Also, the Steelers are coming off a bye while the Bengals are coming off a game in Paris, which is the type of massive rest disadvantage that the NFL should do a better job avoiding. The Bengals are good but this isn't a great matchup or a good spot for them. Ravens (-4.5) over Chargers The Chargers will cover a spread this season. They haven't yet. They are the last team in the NFL to not cover the spread this season. But we'll take that loss when it comes because proactively taking the truly miserable Chargers in hopes they finally cover is not an enjoyable exercise. Also, the Ravens have three days of extra rest and perhaps a little bit of renewed hope with Jacoby Brissett coming aboard. Last week: 9-6 Season to date: 62-71-2

away.headline: 3 thoughts ahead of Vikings' Week 10 game vs. Packers
away.blurb: The Minnesota Vikings have reached the most crucial game of the 2026 season. After the Vikings fell apart on Monday night at home against the Buffalo Bills, there was no reason to think that the Vikings could remain competitive in the NFC North, the best division in the NFL. The Vikings have the best defense in the sport and their special teams are elite. However, their QB play was so brutal that there was nothing for head coach Kevin O’Connell to believe in going forward. With the high-powered Green Bay Packers on deck and the trade deadline coming up hours after the Buffalo embarrassment, the Vikings had to act quickly. By early afternoon, word of their trade with the Las Vegas Raiders emerged. The Vikings were getting Kirk Cousins back in the fold. Their QB1 from 2018 through 2023 was returning. There was palpable relief in the Vikings locker room Justin Jefferson had his greatest success with Cousins at quarterback and he suddenly had hope for the future. Cousins knows how to make the layered throws that O’Connell’s system demands. The presence of Cousins, a competent NFL quarterback and one that had proven himself in the Vikings system, uplifted the confidence level in the Minnesota locker room. Vikings offense does not have to produce immediate miracles Even though Cousins knows O’Connell, Jefferson, Jordan Addison and TE T.J. Hockenson quite well, the Vikings don’t need their quarterback to light up the scoreboard with 300 passing yards and 3 TDs against Green Bay. That would be impressive, but it’s too much to expect in his first couple of weeks back with the Vikings. What Cousins needs to do is string first downs together. The Vikings need to possess the football. The Vikings could not do that against the Lions or Bills in Weeks 8 and 9. The Bills had 42-plus minutes of possession time Monday night. The Vikings defense could not survive that kind of disadvantage. If the Vikings can hold on to the ball for 28, 29 or 30 minutes, the Minnesota defense will not be exhausted in the fourth quarter. That should give Minnesota a fighting chance to compete and possibly win this game. Vikings defense will face significant test The Green Bay Packers are streaking, having won five of their last six games. They have played some of the best offensive football of any team in the league. The 45-27 road victory over the New England Patriots in Week 9 demonstrated how strong the Green Bay passing game is at this point in the season. Jordan Love completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with 3 TDs and he looked unstoppable. WRs Christian Watson and Matthew Golden employed their explosive speed to wreck the Patriots defense. The Vikings have been the best defensive team in the NFL, but the Packers will test them more than any other opponent. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores will rely on the blitz, but he must disguise it in a manner that will cause problems for Love. away.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday's estimates. That doesn't bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We'll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. home.headline: 3 thoughts ahead of Vikings' Week 10 game vs. Packers
home.blurb: The Minnesota Vikings have reached the most crucial game of the 2026 season. After the Vikings fell apart on Monday night at home against the Buffalo Bills, there was no reason to think that the Vikings could remain competitive in the NFC North, the best division in the NFL. The Vikings have the best defense in the sport and their special teams are elite. However, their QB play was so brutal that there was nothing for head coach Kevin O’Connell to believe in going forward. With the high-powered Green Bay Packers on deck and the trade deadline coming up hours after the Buffalo embarrassment, the Vikings had to act quickly. By early afternoon, word of their trade with the Las Vegas Raiders emerged. The Vikings were getting Kirk Cousins back in the fold. Their QB1 from 2018 through 2023 was returning. There was palpable relief in the Vikings locker room Justin Jefferson had his greatest success with Cousins at quarterback and he suddenly had hope for the future. Cousins knows how to make the layered throws that O’Connell’s system demands. The presence of Cousins, a competent NFL quarterback and one that had proven himself in the Vikings system, uplifted the confidence level in the Minnesota locker room. Vikings offense does not have to produce immediate miracles Even though Cousins knows O’Connell, Jefferson, Jordan Addison and TE T.J. Hockenson quite well, the Vikings don’t need their quarterback to light up the scoreboard with 300 passing yards and 3 TDs against Green Bay. That would be impressive, but it’s too much to expect in his first couple of weeks back with the Vikings. What Cousins needs to do is string first downs together. The Vikings need to possess the football. The Vikings could not do that against the Lions or Bills in Weeks 8 and 9. The Bills had 42-plus minutes of possession time Monday night. The Vikings defense could not survive that kind of disadvantage. If the Vikings can hold on to the ball for 28, 29 or 30 minutes, the Minnesota defense will not be exhausted in the fourth quarter. That should give Minnesota a fighting chance to compete and possibly win this game. Vikings defense will face significant test The Green Bay Packers are streaking, having won five of their last six games. They have played some of the best offensive football of any team in the league. The 45-27 road victory over the New England Patriots in Week 9 demonstrated how strong the Green Bay passing game is at this point in the season. Jordan Love completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with 3 TDs and he looked unstoppable. WRs Christian Watson and Matthew Golden employed their explosive speed to wreck the Patriots defense. The Vikings have been the best defensive team in the NFL, but the Packers will test them more than any other opponent. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores will rely on the blitz, but he must disguise it in a manner that will cause problems for Love. home.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday's estimates. That doesn't bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We'll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. home.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? The Jacksonville Jaguars opened Week 10 practice without one of their top receivers. Jakobi Meyers did not practice Wednesday because of an ankle injury, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reported. Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week but played through them. He was on the field for 68 percent of the offensive snaps and caught four passes for 65 yards in the Jaguars' Thursday night win over the Baltimore Ravens. It isn't clear whether the ankle got worse or Wednesday was a maintenance day, but a missed practice is a step back from last week, when he was limited. Running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and defensive end Travon Walker (rib) also did not practice Wednesday , and all three played through those injuries in Baltimore. Trade deadline additions Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out for rest. By our count, Meyers has caught 26 of his 37 targets, a 70.3 percent catch rate, for 374 yards and two touchdowns in eight games, according to ESPN . That works out to 14.4 yards per catch. His season high of 83 receiving yards came against the Houston Texans in London. He followed a two-catch, 24-yard game against the Indianapolis Colts with his 65 yards in Baltimore. Well, technically. The Colts, 2-7, could claim the top spot, but they do not own their own first-round for the next draft, with the New York Jets holding that selection as part of an in-season trade last year that sent cornerback Sauce Gardner to Indianapolis. Despite the Dolphins' positive signs of growth over the past several weeks, the oddsmakers have given the Colts a slight nod in this game. The FanDuel Sportsbook line opened with Indianapolis favored by 2.5 points , slightly under the typical three-point advantage given to a home team, and it has remained steady as of Tuesday morning. The point total is set at 40.5, while Miami is +116 on the money line for the straight-up win. The Colts are -136 for the win. This week could see massive changes in odds as Tuesday's trade deadline approaches. Indianapolis is expected to be sellers today, with running back Jonathan Taylor considered one of the top available players on the market, and rumors swirling around defensive tackle Grover Stewart and quarterback Daniel Jones. If the Colts do start making trades ahead of the 4 p.m. Eastern deadline, how will the line move? Miami could also be sellers, with teams reportedly interested in players like linebacker Jordyn Brooks and defensive tackle Zach Sieler. The Dolphins may not be eager to move on from core pieces of their rebuild, but they may be offered a package of draft picks they cannot refuse. Tuesday could significantly affect the odds for this weekend's game, but for now, the Colts are slightly favored.

(Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jon Spradley · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:56 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts are in trouble, deep trouble. They got close against the Cowboys, but the seventh loss this season marks doom. The Dolphins are coming to town, so this might be their best shot at win number three on the year. FanDuel Sportsbook favors the Colts to start with a 2.5-point spread advantage. The money line is -138 while the over/under sits at 43.5. The Colts had a rough Sunday. As bad as it was, they still had a legitimate chance to pull out a victory. The offense struggled mightily in the first half but put it all together to take a lead with less than two minutes in regulation. The defense that couldn't stop the run to save their lives, gave up a late bomb and touchdown to sink the Colts to 2-7. Speaking of seven, the Dolphins have that many losses too. The Dolphins hung tough against Detroit, finding themselves down 6-3 at the half. Malik Willis' stat line won't win many games, though, as he had 128 yards with no touchdowns, an interception, and three sacks. An uninspiring effort made for an uninspiring final score at 19-9. Neither team wants to pick up loss number eight, at least not yet. The Colts are sinking fast. With their first-round pick belonging to the Jets, they would prefer it doesn't reach higher than it needs to. The team is entering "pride" season, as that is all that may be left to play for. Even a win against the Dolphins may do little to inspire confidence at this point.

It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies NFL experts predict winner of Colts vs. Dolphins Week 10 game Paul Bretl, Colts Wire · Colts Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:12 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Up next for the Indianapolis Colts is a matchup at home against the Miami Dolphins . The Colts enter this game at 2-7, on a five-game losing streak, and with a depleted wide receiver room following the NFL trade deadline. Miami, however, is 1-7 and will have Kyle McCord making his first NFL start at quarterback. Is this the week that the Colts can find a win? Let's check in on who the experts are picking to win this game. A 5-0 sweep in favor of the Colts. Here is why Brooke Cersosimo is picking Indianapolis to win: "Miami's youthful offense, the second-lowest-scoring unit league-wide (15.8 points per game), was slowly building together, and it feels like it's back at square one with McCord under center. This is a real chance for the more experienced Indy squad to get its first win since Oct. 4, and the non-traded Jonathan Taylor is the one with the goods to secure the victory in a low-scoring affair." Pro Football Talk Mike Florio is picking the Colts to win, 17-7. "With the uncertainty of the trade deadline over, the Colts can get back to focusing on trying to win football games." ESPN is more split on this matchup. Five analysts are picking the Colts, while three are taking Miami to win. Pete Prisco has the Colts winning a close one, 23-22. "This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late." Four analysts are picking the Colts while two are taking the Dolphins to win. All six predictors believe it will be a close, one-score game. This article originally appeared on Colts Wire: NFL experts predict winner of Colts vs. Dolphins Week 10 game

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Miami Dolphins (1-7) and Indianapolis Colts (2-7) meet Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium in a matchup between two teams racing towards the top of the 2027 Draft. The Dolphins have lost two straight and sit in the cellar in the AFC East while the Colts have lost five in a row and have only the Titans between them and a spot in the basement in the AFC South. The headline as these teams take the field is that Miami’s starting signal-caller, Malik Willis , has been placed on the IR and as a result, rookie Kyle McCord will get the first start of his career. Indianapolis will continue with Daniel Jones , who has 1,722 passing yards and six touchdowns this season. Jones, however, has struggled to regain the form he had prior to tearing his Achilles late last season. Miami’s latest setback was a 19-9 home loss to the Detroit Lions, a game in which the Dolphins’ defense did enough to give the offense a chance but Miami never reached the end zone. Willis completed just 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards with an interception, while Ollie Gordon II led the Dolphins with 55 rushing yards and Caleb Douglas caught six passes for 70 yards. Miami finished with only 228 total yards, went 0-for-3 in the red zone and settled for three Zane Gonzalez field goals. Indianapolis’ last loss was considerably more painful. The Colts rallied from a 17-7 halftime deficit against Dallas, getting a 55-yard touchdown catch from Ashton Dulin and field goals of 59 and 50 yards from Spencer Shrader to take a 23-20 lead with 1:37 remaining. But Dak Prescott immediately hit Ryan Flournoy for 46 yards, and Javonte Williams scored from a yard out with 1:08 left to give Dallas a 27-23 victory. Jones finished 20-of-34 for 180 yards, a touchdown and an interception, while Jonathan Taylor managed only 46 yards on 13 carries and lost a costly fourth-quarter fumble. Dallas piled up 508 yards to Indianapolis’ 271, illustrating the biggest concern for a Colts’ team that is allowing 361.8 yards and 27.7 points per game. The central storyline, then, is which struggling offense can take advantage of an accommodating opponent. Miami is averaging only 15.8 points per game, 31st in the league, and will be asking McCord to make his debut on the road; Indianapolis averages 20.4 points but carries a -11 turnover differential, making ball security especially important for Jones and Taylor. Recent history favors the Colts. Indianapolis has won the last three meetings, including a 33-8 rout at Lucas Oil Stadium in Week 1 of the 2025 season, when Jones completed 22 of 29 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown and Taylor rushed for 71 yards. The broader history belongs to the Dolphins, who hold a 48-30 advantage across 78 regular-season and postseason meetings. away.headline: Examining the Looming Dolphins Roster Moves After the Week 9 Final Injury Report
away.blurb: The good news for the Miami Dolphins with their final injury report for Week 9 is they didn't rule out any players for the matchup against the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium. The team did list three players as questionable and it might require some roster juggling Saturday. In fact, it probably will require it. The three players listed as questionable were running backs Jaylen Wright and Kaytron Allen, both of whom are dealing with a quad injury, and defensive end Malik Herring, who has a neck issue after sustaining a stinger in the Week 8 loss against the New England Patriots. It's also possible the Dolphins don't have to do anything beyond elevating Gonzalez if the three players listed as questionable are deemed fit and ready to go against Detroit before the deadline. As expected, Kadyn Proctor has gotten out of the concussion protocol and will be back in the lineup against the Lions. Along with the three questionable players, the only other one who was limited in practice Friday was long-snapper Tucker Addington with his ongoing shoulder issue. For Detroit, the big news was safety Brian Branch being cleared out of the concussion protocol and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown The one update for them involved backup running back Sione Vaki, who popped up on the injury report and did not practice Friday. He was listed as questionable. Detroit ruled out five players, including safety Kerby Joseph, who's on IR, and obviously linebacker Jack Campbell, who sustained a serious neck injury against the Minnesota Vikings last Sunday. The others were center Cade Mays, cornerback D.J. Reed and edge DJ Wonnum. Examining the Looming Dolphins Roster Moves After the Week 9 Final Injury Report Skip to main content SI.COM Wright and Allen are the two backups at running back behind new starter Ollie Gordon II (with De'Von Achane on IR) and it would seem almost a given that the Dolphins will be elevating Carlos Washington Jr. as insurance. The Dolphins also need a kicker and the only one they have also is on the practice squad, that being veteran Zane Gonzalez. And lastly, the Dolphins have operated with five edge defenders every game and if Herring can't play, that would leave them with four — Chop Robinson, Josh Uche, Rodney McGraw and newcomer Jamree Kromah. Max Llewellyn was elevated from the practice squad for the game against New England, but that was his third elevation. That means the Dolphins can't use him again this season unless they sign him to the 53-man roster, which certainly appears to be a possibility since they've kept him on the practice squad. Other practice squad options if Herring can't play would be elevating either Amari Gaither or Eric Watts from the practice squad. Signing Gonzalez to the 53 is another option, even though he did have a bad field goal miss against New England. Dolphins Week 9 Final Injury Report: 3 Players Questionable Miami will have its hands full, but the good news for the team is that they will not have many players out for the matchup. The vast majority of the players who were limited on Thursday were upgraded to full participants on Friday, giving them no injury status for the Lions matchup. Long snapper Tucker Addington was not upgraded and remained limited through Friday with a shoulder injury, but he has no status for the game. There are three players who remain questionable for the contest. Running back Jaylen Wright is dealing with a quad injury and was limited on Thursday and Friday, leaving him questionable. Fellow running back Kaytron Allen was limited Wednesday and Thursday, but was upgraded on Friday with a quad injury. He is also questionable. Finally, edge Malik Herring is dealing with a neck injury and was limited all week. Herring might be a player that is most likely to not play against the Lions. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed that Proctor would return in Week 9 after missing Week 8 due to entering the concussion protocol. Proctor revealed that he had been suffering from dizziness following Week 7, leading to being placed in the protocol. Per the injury report, Brown is dealing with a rib injury and is also questionable for the game. Should he not be able to play, the Dolphins will catch a big break not having to defend the dynamic pass catcher. It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Saints Rookie Report: Week 10 preview vs. the Panthers NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints avoids a tackle Ronnie Hickman #33 of the Cleveland Browns during a game at Caesars Superdome on November 08, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A big game is right around the corner for the New Orleans Saints, and hopefully, after the trade deadline, the rookies can lead the Saints to a win. WR Jordyn Tyson It was an exciting debut for Tyson. Yes, he fumbled on his first catch, but it was a really great play by the Browns defender, and Tyson will learn not to reach like that if he is not close enough to the end zone. But after that, when he was able to play, Tyson was open every time he was on the field and picked up some very important yards. Per head coach Kellen Moore, Tyson will have a larger role in the offense in Week 10, and he could have an incredible performance against the Panthers. DT Christen Miller I really do not know what to say anymore. Miller was a healthy scratch on Sunday. I wish there was more clarity on this situation because it makes zero sense why he is not playing. Miller has been a whelming run defender and has made little impact in pass rush, which is perfectly fine. He needs to play more. Hopefully, after the Davon Godchaux trade, Miller can have more snaps, even if he's not the starter. TE Oscar Delp I hoped that Delp would be more involved in the offense, but that didn't happen. Maybe if he were the receiver instead of Noah Fant on that drop, the Saints would have scored a touchdown on that play. The Saints need to start prioritizing the youth on this roster, and I'm hoping Delp can finally get some consistent targets against the Panthers. OG Jeremiah Wright News on Cesar Ruiz's injury has not been released yet, so it's unknown if Wright is going play, but if he does, good luck to him. The Browns defensive line is very good, and it's going to be his biggest test yet. He wasn't horrible against the Steelers, but it was also not good, and he looked like a rookie out there. That's the expectation, but the Saints will need to see more from him against the Browns. WR Bryce Lance It's time for Lance to be benched and not involved in the offense. He was thrown to once and dropped the ball, which completely stalled the drive and was outperformed by his fellow rookie WRs. Lance is a good blocker, but he's making consistent mistakes. WR Barion Brown Now to Brown; he had a much better day. Like with Tyson, Brown made a really bad mistake that resulted in a fumble, but outside of that, he had a great day. Brown was getting the Saints in great field position on nearly every return and had a 50+ yard catch in this game. I'm hoping that Brown can take over Lance's snaps and potentially get a few catches against the Panthers. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson has been injured and is lower on the depth chart now. OT Mason Murphy It seems like Kelvin Banks Jr. is on his way back, so Murphy's chances of starting become even lower. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. As usual, Styles will likely stick with the special teams unit, but it will be interesting to see what happens if Justin Reid gets traded.

away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. away.headline: Carolina Panthers vs. Broncos: Who will win? Predictions, injury report, TV info
away.blurb: Out: CB Will Lee (hamstring), G Damien Lewis (knee), LB Bobby Okereke (foot), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), OL Brady Christensen (hamstring)* Questionable: OL Corey Bullock (quad), OL Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) Out: CB Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), S Brandon Jones (hamstring), DL Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder) Questionable: WR Pat Bryant (ankle), OLB Dondrea Tilman (hip), S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) Alex Zietlow: Broncos 31, Panthers 21. The Panthers will be experimenting a bunch this week. They’ll presumably shake the personnel up along the offensive line, and they’ll have a new defensive coach calling plays. Such risks might work out for them, kind of like how their RPOs stunned the Lions’ defense on Sunday Night Football (gosh, that feels like a lifetime ago!). Even still, I think the Broncos are too talented on defense and too disciplined on offense to let a winnable game like this slip away. Sunday, they’ll want to steady the ship. And they will have to pull off an upset to do so. The Panthers (3-4) still sit atop the NFC South, but in order to hold onto their station, they’ll likely need to emerge from Bank of America Stadium with a victory against one of the powers of the AFC — the Denver Broncos (6-2). The Sean Payton-led team has won its last four contests, including a 28-24 thriller against the Chiefs. Another flattering Broncos stat: They’re 15-0 in their last 15 regular-season one-score games . Here’s a one-stop shop for everything you need to know ahead of the contest, including score predictions, betting odds, injury statuses and more. TV, radio information for Panthers-Packers The Panthers’ Week 9 matchup will begin at 1 p.m. Sunday in uptown Charlotte’s largest venue. It’ll be broadcast on CBS; Ian Eagle will do the play-by-play, with Ross Tucker as the analyst and Evan Washburn as the sideline reporter. Fans can also catch the game on the radio: WRFX The Fox: 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline reporter). Check the Panthers Radio Network for full listings. Spanish Radio: WXNC 97.3 FM, 1060 AM. Jaime Moreno (play-by-play), Antonio Ramos (analyst). Betting odds for Carolina-Denver game The Panthers are 2.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook on Sunday morning . The over/under for the contest is 44.5 points. The Panthers are 3-4 against the spread so far this season. The Broncos are 6-2. Broncos head coach Sean Payton has a long history in the NFC South. That included a Super Bowl in New Orleans. Payton’s record against the Panthers, according to Pro Football Reference, is 19-13, including the only win as Broncos head coach against the Panthers in 2024. Some more connections between the programs: Ejiro Evero had a successful stint as defensive coordinator in Denver prior to coming over to Carolina; Evero was fired from the Panthers last week; Sunday will mark Todd Wash’s debut as interim defensive coordinator and play caller. home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Three Remain Sidelined, Etienne Participates for Second Consecutive Day
home.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? Center Erik McCoy (biceps) missed his second consecutive practice , while offensive tackles Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and Taliese Fuaga remained limited. Guard David Edwards (knee) was also limited. Running back Alvin Kamara (back) returned to full participation after taking his weekly rest day, while tight end Noah Fant (back) also upgraded to full participation. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) remained limited, leaving his availability uncertain as he continues to make his first appearance since its week 3 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders . Defensively, rookie defensive tackle Christen Miller (knee) was downgraded to a nonparticipant after practicing on a limited basis Wednesday. Cornerbacks Martin Emerson Jr. (shin) and Quincy Riley were limited. Overall, the Saints listed 12 players on Thursday's injury report, including three who did not practice. Friday's final injury report will provide a clearer picture of which players could be unavailable against Carolina. As for the Carolina Panthers, it had just one player miss Thursday's practice, with linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) sitting out for the second consecutive day. Defensive end Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and offensive guard Damien Lewis (knee) were limited, while Chuba Hubbard (rest), Jonathon Brooks (groin), Brady Christensen (hamstring), Mike Jackson (groin), Will Lee III (hamstring) and Xavier Legette (knee) participated fully ahead of Sunday's matchup against the New Orleans Saints. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 1:42 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their fourth straight game and seventh of their last eight on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They kept it competitve for a half. In the first half the Jets outgained the Chiefs. They won the turnover battle. They had more than twice the time of possession as the Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 – 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 – 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. Regardless, if the Jets don't exit next week with their eighth loss of the season it will be a major surprise. Join Gang Green Nation on game day! Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. Buffalo has won eight of the past 10 meetings, including a couple smacks last season, beating the Jets 30-10 at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 14, 2025 and 35-8 in Buffalo on Jan. 4, 2026. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. It was more of the same for the Jets last Sunday as they were shut out in the second half in another blowout loss − a 35-12 defeat at the hands of Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. The Jets, on a four-game losing streak, welcome in the Buffalo Bills , who are 7-1 and currently the No. 1 seed in the AFC coming off Monday night's impressive 23-6 victory on the road over the Minnesota Vikings . Like most opponents, the Jets have failed to keep up with the Bills in recent meetings. Gang Green has dropped five straight games against Buffalo and have been outscored, 160-58, in the process. The Bills have averaged 32 points per game over that time and the Jets have been unable to score 21 or more points in any of those contests. It'll be another uphill battle for the Jets, who were swept by the Bills in 2026, with Buffalo winning by three or more scores both times last season.
