picks.headline: Bills vs Jets prediction and key matchups for tricky division game
picks.blurb: News Sports Life Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals BILLS Bills vs Jets prediction and key matchups for tricky division game Sal Maiorana Rochester Democrat and Chronicle Nov. 13, 2026, 3:50 a.m. ET ORCHARD PARK - If there was a moment when the team-wide frustration that the New York Jets have experienced this season boiled to a head, it was last Sunday in Kansas City when quarterback Geno Smith momentarily lost his mind. In the second quarter of what became their fourth straight loss, the Jets were leading 9-7 when Braelon Allen lost a fumble that was recovered by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman. As Gilman began his return, Smith rushed over and launched himself with intent and knocked Gilman flat at the Jets 24, a stunning display of physicality from a quarterback. “It's something that you really don't want to happen, but competitors are going to compete, so I'm not surprised that it happened, but that's something that you don't want from your starting quarterback,” coach Aaron Glenn said. Smith knew the fumble was a huge mistake and sure enough, the Chiefs scored two plays later and grabbed a lead they never relinquished in their 35-12 blowout. Later in the game, following another failed Jets possession, Smith came to the sideline and slammed his helmet to the ground, the inevitability of falling to 2-7 clearly getting to him. As usual in mid-November, the Jets are already in playing-out-the-string mode, but they have a great chance to make a statement Sunday when they host the 7-1 Buffalo Bills . There isn’t too much left to play for downstate, but beating the AFC’s No. 1 team and damaging the Bills’ quest for the No. 1 seed would certainly provide some professional joy, especially considering the two 30-10 and 35-8 beatings Buffalo put on New York last year. “We're not going to hide from the fact that we're 2-7,” said Glenn, who is likely coaching for his job so every possible victory is crucial. “We own that, but man, we're still working our (butts) off to make sure we fix that. We like the players that we have in the building to be able to help us do that. When you look at the seven losses, and this is just the facts, five of the teams were playoff-caliber teams. I think five of them were one-score games. There's a number of things that we got to fix and get better at, but we feel like, man, we're right on the cusp of trying to break through.” Joe Brady claims he never pays attention to the standings or an opponent’s record, but he knows the Jets are 2-7, and he also knows that a few plays here or there could have altered the course of their season. He and his team won’t be taking a division opponent lightly. “This is a division game on the road, it's going to be as hard as it gets, right?” Brady said. “We’ve showed that we can go on the road and win a hard game (actually seven straight dating to 2025), we got to go do it again. (Glenn’s) going to have them ready to go as he should. We know we're always gonna get everybody's best as we should, and we're gonna have to bring it to be able to come out with a win. We know it's not gonna be easy, but we wouldn't want it any other way.” Here’s my preview of the game, followed by my prediction: The QB Matchup: Josh Allen vs. Geno Smith One of the reasons why Allen continues to be perhaps the best QB in the league is the way he has been able to adapt to whatever is required to win a game. Some weeks he has needed to throw the ball downfield and bite off big chunks, in others he needed to stay patient and work underneath. Some games he needed to use his legs to jump start the offense, in others he needed to lean on James Cook and the running game. “Everything starts with the quarterback,” Glenn said. “He's playing at a high level, which he always does, so we're looking forward to the competition.” Allen is tied for the league lead at 8.6 yards per attempt and is second in yards per completion at 13.0, yet his 99.3 passer rating is a smidge less than Smith who has been better than the Jets’ record would indicate. Smith’s 100.5 passer rating through nine weeks is the highest by a Jets quarterback at this point of a season since the 1970 merger. He’s completing 67.5% of his passes which ranks fifth in the league and his 1.1% interception rate is fourth-best, so this is not going to be Joe Fagnano or Carson Wentz that the Bills’ defense is facing. Buffalo Bills who should impact the game ▶ TE Dalton Kincaid: The best part of Kincaid’s season thus far is that he has played in every game, something that had been an issue for him the previous two seasons. He has 30 catches for 429 yards and two TDs, but again, you long for more. His 14.3 yards per catch is second-best among TEs behind only Travis Kelce (14.6), so Allen needs to start finding ways to get him the ball beyond the 38 targets he’s seen. ▶ C Connor McGovern: The Jets defense ranks 26th in the league allowing 128 rushing yards per game and has been gouged for 29 runs of at least 10 yards, tied for the fourth-most in the league. McGovern and the rest of the Bills’ line has paved the way for the second-best rushing attack fronted by Cook, and given the Jets’ 39.9% blitz rate, sixth-highest in the league per Next Gen Stats, the Bills would love to catch them with quick hitters through the A and B gaps. ▶ DT Ed Oliver: He started to knock some rust off against Minnesota and played his best game of the season. He had seven pressures and for the season, Sumer Sports has him charted for 109 pass rush snaps and his 19.3% pressure rate is No. 1 among interior linemen. And though he’s only had 45 run snaps, he has been very effective with a 15.6% run stop percentage which is second-best. But Oliver and the rest of the D-line has a big test against a solid Jets offensive line. ▶ CB Dee Alford: After a rough start to his Bills career, Alford played his best game in Minnesota and was part of the reason why Wentz was so awful. But this will be a bigger test as the Jets have been using impressive WR Omar Cooper in the slot on about half his snaps and Cooper has been one of the best players in this rookie class. Alford will also find himself against the two Jets TEs who have excelled thus far, Mason Taylor and rookie matchup nightmare Kenyon Sadiq. New York Jets who should impact the game ▶ RB Braelon Allen: He pounced on an opportunity while No. 1 RB Breece Hall was sidelined for five weeks and in those games, Allen averaged 101 yards rushing, 5.4 yards per attempt, and caught 13 passes for 70 yards. Hall returned last week against the Chiefs and ran for 68 yards despite playing 10 fewer snaps than Allen, and that seems to be an indication that the Jets will use both players in a rotation and that gives them an opportunity to play ball control and keep the Bills’ offense off the field. ▶ WR Garrett Wilson: He leads the Jets with 43 catches for 527 yards and three TDs despite missing last week’s game with a concussion, but his numbers would be even better if Smith utilized him more. Wilson has had five games where he was targeted seven times or fewer and that’s not ideal for a player who has big-play ability. Part of this is because the Jets have two other WRs in Cooper and Adonai Mitchell, and TEs Sadiq and Taylor who have made nice contributions, but Wilson needs more targets. ▶ LB David Bailey: The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 draft looks like a star in the making already and he’s going to present problems off the edge. He has 7.5 sacks and 31 QB pressures which lead the team, his 20 stops (plays that caused a failure for the offense) are second to LB Jamien Sherwood, and his five forced fumbles are the main reason the Jets lead the league with 13 total. Bailey lines up almost exclusively to the offense’s right, so RT Spencer Brown, now battling an ankle injury as well as a cranky back, will have a big challenge dealing with Bailey’s explosive speed. ▶ S Minkah Fitzpatrick: He has become a big-time rival for the Bills as he has faced them eight times during his time with the Steelers and his two stints with the Dolphins. Now he’s with the Jets and he’s still at the top of his game and is one reason why the Jets have played pretty good pass defense. He has allowed just six receptions on 12 targets, and his 33 snaps per reception allowed is fifth-best among all safeties. Sal’s prediction: Bills 30, Jets 20 It’s hard to get to a place where I can think the Jets can pull the upset. Of course, I felt the same way in 2022 when a 6-1 Bills team went to New Jersey and lost 20-17, and in 2023 when Aaron Rodgers got hurt on the fourth play of the game and the Bills still found a way to lose. Even in 2024, it was all the Bills could do to pull out a 23-20 victory on a late Tyler Bass field goal. My point is division games on the road are tough. Remember last year in Miami? The Bills will need to be on point against a New York team that has a lousy record, but has emerging talent on both sides of the ball, especially on offense. In the end, with the Bills’ offense functioning at such a high rate, I don’t think the red zone-challenged Jets can keep pace. away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. JSN is coming off a relatively quiet performance against the Cardinals, finishing with seven catches for 51 yards without a touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 tracker: Injury updates, prediction, storylines and more - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Scores / Schedules Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald is seen before a game | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Lee Vowell · 12th Man Rising Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads About our Ads The Seattle Seahawks are 5-4 and head to Las Vegas to play the 4-5 Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Week 10. Seattle will be playing with a backup quarterback, Drew Lock, and Las Vegas will have a rookie quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, in his first career start. Head coach Mike Macdonald's team still has the better roster, and should be expected to win, but the Raiders are better this season than in quite some time. A victory against Seattle would be huge for their collective confidence. Health could be a factor. Seattle's injury report was fairly lengthy, so even some players who perform in Week 10 might not be close to 100 percent. At least, the bye week follows in Week 11. Seattle Seahawks injury updates for Week 10 Anthony Bradford Charles Cross Ribs and quad Elbow and oblique Quenton Nelson Uchenna Nwosu Patrick O'Connell Connor O'Toole Personal matter Rashid Shaheed Jaxon Smith-Njigba Leonard Williams Sam Darnold has already been ruled out, so he won't play. Drew Lock was expected to be limited all week, but is expected to play in Week 10. Leonard Williams is already trending toward missing another game. He will be missed. Seattle will announce its full list of inactives an hour and a half before kickoff, and this article will be updated with the latest information. Raiders inactives and injury updates Thomas Booker Foley Fatukasi Shoulder and back Trey Zuhn III The Raiders are fairly healthy, but what doesn't show on their injury report is the trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. This means rookie Fernando Mendoza will start for the first time in the NFL. As with Seattle, Vegas will announce its inactives an hour and a half before kickoff. How to watch Seahawks vs. Raiders in Week 10 Date: Sunday, November 15 Time: 1:05 p.m. PT TV Network: CBS (KIRO 7 in Seattle) Announcers: Ian Eagle (play-by-play), Ross Tucker (analysis), and Evan Washburn (sideline reporter) In the Seattle area, you can also stream the game on NFL+, while nationally, you might need a subscription to YouTube TV's NFL Sunday Ticket to stream or watch the game. You can listen to the game on the Seahawks Mobile App, SiriusXM channels 123 or 269, Seattle Sports 710 AM, and KIRO Newsradio 97.3. Steve Raible will provide the play-by-play for the Seahawks broadcast, while Dave Wyman will do the analysis, and Jen Mueller will report from the sidelines. Storylines to watch for Seahawks in Week 10 How will Fernando Mendoza do? Obviously, what most national fans will be interested in is how well the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft will do in his first career start . While Vegas trading Kirk Cousins made sense, Mendoza's first two starts couldn't come against tougher defenses: The Seahawks and then the Denver Broncos. Presumably, head coach Klint Kubiak isn't going to let Mendoza throw the ball 50 times, but he could have a somewhat conservative game plan to operate with. Kubiak is a good coach, so fans should expect a difficult challenge, even against a rookie quarterback. Will Drew Lock succeed against a non-Arizona Cardinals team? The difference between Lock games and Sam Darnold games has been significant this season. Lock has turned the ball over in three games. Darnold has nine interceptions in six games. What fans have seen from Lock might not be reality, though. He played the majority of reps in Week 1 against the New England Patriots, but Week 1s are often lies. His other two games have been against the terrible Cardinals. Darnold has faced far tougher competition. Lock's true first test might come against the Raiders, who are eighth in the league with seven interceptions. Can the Seahawks succeed running the ball? Week 9 against the Cardinals looked quite a bit different offensively for Seattle. That is partly because running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were healthier. To win with Lock, and even when Darnold returns, the running game needs to continue being good. The Raiders are tight for last in the NFL at allowing 5.0 yards per carry. They are also last in yards allowed per rushing attempt at 151.2. The Seahawks must run the ball effectively to win. Prediction for Week 10 Seahawks 21, Raiders 14 This game is difficult to predict due to a number of factors, including how good Mendoza might be and the overall health of the Seahawks' defense. If Leonard Williams and Uchenna Nwosu miss the game again, the normally lofty standard of Mike Macdonald's defense could be exposed by a good offensive coach for Las Vegas. The hope is that Seattle wins a fairly ugly game, one that will probably be close until the end. Hopefully, Drew Lock just plays another clean game. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Seattle Seahawks (5-4) head to Las Vegas on Sunday trying to establish some momentum in a tightly packed NFC West race, while the Raiders (4-5) are looking to rebound from one of their sloppiest performances of the season AND are looking to do so with rookie Fernando Mendoza making his first start of his career. The matchup is a monster challenge for Mendoza: Seattle has leaned on a defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth-best in the league entering the week, while Las Vegas has surrendered 29.8 per game, ranking last. So you expect the Raiders would look to lean on Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. to run the ball and take the pressure off their rookie signal-caller…but know that the Seahawks allow an average of 89.1 yards per game (151.2 for the Raiders). Quarterback is also a storyline for the Seahawks. Sam Darnold remains sidelined with a quad injury after also reportedly cracking a rib against Chicago, while Drew Lock came out of this past Sunday’s game dealing with an oblique issue after previously battling elbow tendinitis. Seattle comes in off a much-needed 17-3 victory over Arizona, a game it controlled despite playing without starting quarterback Darnold. Backup Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown, while tight end AJ Barner supplied both Seattle touchdowns, catching one from Lock and running for another. Zach Charbonnet , recently returned from an ACL injury, gave the offense some balance with 77 yards on 16 carries, and the defense held Arizona to 216 total yards and no touchdowns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught seven passes for 51 yards and became the first NFL receiver to reach 1,000 yards this season. Las Vegas, meanwhile, is trying to clean up the turnovers after a 38-17 loss at San Francisco dropped it below .500. The Raiders were actually within 21-10 at halftime, but Kirk Cousins was intercepted on the first play of the third quarter and Jaden Dugger returned it 35 yards for a touchdown, beginning a disastrous second half. Cousins finished 22-of-32 for 216 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions as Las Vegas committed five turnovers, managed only 240 total yards and 24 rushing yards, and possessed the ball for just 21:42. Brock Bowers was possibly the only bright spot, catching seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown. Sunday’s game is also a reunion of two franchises with considerably more history than their present-day conference alignment suggests. The Raiders and Seahawks were AFC West rivals from 1977 through 2001, and the Raiders lead the overall series 30-26, including postseason games. They have met only periodically since Seattle moved to the NFC, with the last meeting producing one of the wildest games of the 2022 season: the Raiders won 40-34 in overtime in Seattle, powered by Josh Jacobs’ 229 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Whoever is under center will once again be working with a patchwork offensive line as stars Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross did not practice. Nelson is battling a knee injury that might hold him out for his second straight game while Cross has been out with an ankle injury since Week 7. Backup guard Anthony Bradford continues to be hampered by a knee injury and was limited on Wednesday. On the defensive side, Leonard Williams remains out with a stinger that he suffered against the Kansas City Chiefs, and edge rusher Derick Hall was limited with a new back injury. Both would be a massive loss for the Seahawks front that will hope to ruin Raiders' rookie Fernando Mendoza's debut. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The favorites in August to claim the Lombardi Trophy, the LA Rams (5-4) currently sit on the wrong side of the playoff bubble as they prepare to take on the Arizona Cardinals (3-6) Sunday in Glendale. The Rams’ struggles are the result of injuries and consistently inconsistent play. That said, they take the field riding a three-game winning streak that has pushed them into a tie with Seatle for second in the NFC West. The Cardinals are last in the division as a result of losses two of the last three weeks. Los Angeles has climbed back into the playoff chase behind Matthew Stafford , who has thrown for 2,374 yards and 16 touchdowns. Arizona averages only 19.8 points per game while surrendering 28.3, but there is one significant reason the Rams won’t take the Cardinals lightly: Arizona already beat them 18-16 on Oct. 18 at SoFi Stadium. Los Angeles extended its winning streak to three last Sunday with a 20-13 road victory over the Washington Commanders. The Rams’ defense has been central to the turnaround, holding the Chargers to nine points and Washington to 13 in consecutive weeks, and Los Angeles enters Sunday allowing only 20.1 points and 312.9 yards per game. The major concern is what Stafford will have around him. Star receiver Puka Nacua , the team’s leading receiver with 715 yards, is out after suffering knee and toe injuries, while Davante Adams remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and tight end Terrance Ferguson is also sidelined. It is up to Head Coach Sean McVay and Stafford to keep the offense functioning even with several of its most important weapons sidelined. Arizona’s most recent outing was far less encouraging. The Cardinals followed up a thrilling and improbable 33-30 overtime win in Dallas with a 17-3 loss at Seattle. The Cardinals are now 3-6 and, remarkably, 0-3 at home, while an offense already struggling for consistency is undergoing a major change at quarterback. With Gardner Minshew placed on injured reserve, rookie Carson Beck is set to make his first appearance against the Rams, putting even more importance on running back Tyler Allgeier and tight end Trey McBride , who leads Arizona with 598 receiving yards and five touchdown catches. The recent history makes this matchup particularly interesting because as noted earlier, Arizona has already pulled off one of the season’s bigger divisional upsets. On Oct. 18, the Cardinals went into SoFi Stadium and beat the Rams 18-16 despite failing to score a touchdown, riding six field goals from Chad Ryland . Los Angeles took a 16-15 lead with 46 seconds remaining on a Stafford touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson , only for Arizona to drive back into field-goal range and win on Ryland’s 43-yarder as time expired. That result interrupted what had otherwise been a Rams-dominated stretch in the rivalry: Los Angeles beat Arizona 45-17 in December 2025 and 37-20 in January 2026, and the Rams lead the complete series 53-42-2, including a 2-0 postseason record. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.headline: Rams went for the big fish at the NFL trade deadline amid injuries on offense and you can't blame the organization for trying
away.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? It would have been a fascinating move. McConkey has been one of the better wide receivers in the NFL, even with modest numbers this season. He has 17 receptions for 286 yards and one touchdown in six games. That being said, he's still averaging a career-high 11.9 yards per target while stuck in an abysmal offense. Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert have struggled to form a connection in Year 1 working together, and it hasn't been easy for anyone in that offense. According to the A to Z Sports Trade Simulator , the price for McConkey would have been somewhere in the ball park of multiple Day 2 selections considering the Rams have limited draft picks to work with. Regardless, the Chargers weren't budging on McConkey and you can't blame the Rams for stepping up and taking a swing, even if they struck out. The call didn't produce a deal before the 1 p.m. PT deadline on Tuesday. Even so, the effort speaks volumes about where the Rams' heads were at. They weren't going to stand pat with this many injuries piling up. Puka Nacua suffered a knee and toe injuries, specifically an MCL and PCL sprains plus a turf toe injury. He's expected back off IR around Weeks 14-15 and hasn't yet been placed on the injured reserve. Jordan Whittington, however, was placed on the IR with a back injury that continued to flare up. "Being on IR means you must miss at least four games, not weeks, and the Rams have a bye in Week 11. So, if they think it's possible Nacua might only have to miss four weeks, they could refrain from putting him on IR and possibly have him back in time for their Week 14 game at San Francisco," ESPN's Dan Graziano said. "This all becomes moot if they put Nacua on IR this week, but just keep an eye on the situation if they don't." Davante Adams has also been sidelined with a hamstring injury. His return window looks similar, around Week 14. The Rams' injury bug also hit the tight end room. Terrance Ferguson, a player the team likes a lot for the versatility he brings in the receiving game, is dealing with a hamstring injury of his own. He's set to miss another couple of weeks. With four key pass catchers out, it's easy to see why the Rams picked up the phone. So, where does that leave the Rams? The wide receiver room now consists of Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, and Tutu Atwell. That isn't a good group by any means. Mumpfield leads the way for that group with only 162 receiving yards on the season. Atwell has 99, and Whittington has just 12. Clearly, the Rams have a glaring problem at wide receiver. One would think the offense leans into a lot more multi-tight end sets with Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, and Davis Allen moving forward. Bleacher Report • 12h Jameis Yells 'Who Let the Dogs Out' 🐶 Justin Herbert reportedly wasn't the only player about whom the winless Los Angeles Chargers rebuffed trade inquiries ahead of Tuesday's deadline. The Los Angeles Rams are believed to have asked after wide receiver Ladd McConkey following the injuries that have sidelined Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday. "The Chargers said no to at least one Ladd McConkey inquiry," Fowler reported. "Teams I spoke to believe the Rams were the ones to make that call." The news comes after NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Minnesota Vikings expressed interest in trading for Herbert before the Chargers "immediately shut down all inquiries." McConkey, who is under contract through 2027, has gone from serving as Herbert's top target last season to recording just 17 catches with 286 yards and a touchdown in six games with the struggling Chargers' offense. He missed his second game of the season last Sunday after suffering back spasms ahead of kickoff against the Houston Texans. The Rams still might have hoped a fresh start for McConkey would help the wide receiver would help add some depth around Stafford in a campaign during which he has yet to play up to his 2025 MVP form. Nacua could be hoping for a similar timeline given that the wide receiver has not yet been placed on injured reserve, although Rams coach Sean McVay has said the team expects to lose him for at least a month with an MCL and PCL sprain as well as turf toe in his right leg. But these teams meet in Week 10 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Entering with a record of 7-1, the 49ers sit as the No. 1 in the NFC. Meanwhile, the Cowboys are trying to fight their way back into contention in the NFC East. They have a record of 4-5. The 49ers are road favorites, but only by 3.5 points. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 250 yards and two TD passes It's a matter of scheme that Purdy will have success , according to ESPN. "Kyle Shanahan will have answers for both the run and pass game Sunday in Dallas," Matt Bowen wrote. "Schemed throws for Brock Purdy that create open coverage voids off play-action, plus a multiple run game with Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to attack a Cowboys defense, allowing 5.0 YPC (third most). I like the 49ers to cover on the road." Purdy has thrown for 1,980 yards this season with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions. He has been impressive and has the eye of head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to a post on X by 95.7 TheGame via Heavy.com. "Yeah, it's been amazing," Shanahan said. "Just since the first game he got in there. That's why I struggle at the beginning of the year when everyone's asking me, can I believe how good he's playing and how much better he's improved because he was so good off the bench versus Miami in his first game and the second week… taking us to the NFC Championship as a rookie. "And I think his second year took us to the Super Bowl maybe. So Brock's been the man since he's come in, and it's pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started… very fortunate to have Brock." The Cowboys will have their hands full. Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb will get 8-plus catches and 90-plus yards The Cowboys are going to get the ball to Lamb. It's their best path to having a shot at beating the 49ers. Lamb left the win over the Colts with a sigh of relief, according to dallascowboys.com. "Those are the games that you love to end up on top," Lamb said. "We understand it was the same situation that we were kind of in last week, and we didn't end up on top then, so just finishing out the game, finishing out the drive — shout out to the defense for ending the game. "But I think I had, like, three penalties alone in the second half, and a fumble. Personally, I gotta take a real good look. The numbers look crazy, but it could have been more. And I'm always thinking about what could have been. So, as for me, as a leader on this offense,I feel like I've got to be better in some realms and just end the game." The 49ers are off to a great start. But before the season, the Cowboys were in the same conversation with them. Lamb said the Cowboys need to get the job done. "We know what we got going on, just the history of that [matchup], the guys that they have over there on defense and the prep, I mean, it's going to take a lot of a lot of preparation, and a lot of execution," Lamb said. "We can't have as many flags because they have a really good offense, too." Prescott will lean heavily on Lamb if George Pickens misses another game. But even if Pickens plays, Prescott won't forget who he needs to target, early and often. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey will get in the end zone twice Look for McCaffrey to score on the ground and with a reception. The 49ers are going to get him the ball near the goal line. One thing that helps McCaffrey's overall usage is that Shanahan is more confident that he is ready to rock after a pre-bye injury slowed him somewhat, according to ninerswire.com. "No. I actually forgot about it," Shanahan said. "He had a good bye week, and he told me before the bye week in Christian style not to worry about it at all. He'll be fine, and he looked good all week." McCaffrey hasn't had a blowout game all season. His rushing high is 75 yards, and his receiving high is 61. But he has 10 total touchdowns, with nine of them coming off the ground. And consistency has been a hallmark. McCaffrey has scored in seven straight games. In three of those contests, he scored twice. The 49ers will need to be sharp offensively. Despite the way their defense has played, they will have trouble slowing down the Cowboys' high-octane offense. McCaffrey will likely need those scores to keep his team in good business. The contrast extends beyond the standings is explained in the numbers: the 49ers are averaging 29.4 points per game while allowing 19.5, compared with 27.3 scored and 26.2 allowed by the Cowboys. San Francisco arrives in Arlington following a convincing 38-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a game the 49ers broke open with a turnover-fueled second half. Brock Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Christian McCaffrey scored once on the ground and once through the air. San Francisco led 21-10 at halftime before Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown on the Raiders’ first offensive play of the third quarter. away.blurb: The good news is that ESPN's Nick Wagoner noted that it sounded like Lenoir and Green participated in Thursday morning's walkthrough, which the media could not observe. That suggests that both might be trending towards being available on Sunday. During his Thursday interview on Bay Area radio station KNBR, head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked whether Lenoir and Green need to practice to play in a game. The question was about Green and cornerback Upton Stout , but the latter was likely mentioned by mistake instead of Lenoir, as Stout has been practicing—albeit as a limited participant—this week. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel returned to practice Wednesday after missing three games with a hamstring injury. He was back on the field Thursday, putting him closer to a potential return against Dallas. It's also worth noting that linebacker Dre Greenlaw and tackle Trent Williams were limited participants. Greenlaw is listed with a knee injury, while Williams is dealing with a shoulder issue. Neither practiced on Wednesday, which was designated a rest day for both. away.headline: Cowboys Get Encouraging Joey Porter Jr. Injury Update Ahead of 49ers Matchup
away.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? The Dallas Cowboys could be getting an important piece of their secondary back at the right time. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is making progress in his recovery from an ankle injury, giving the team some hope that he could return for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. Porter has dealt with an interrupted start to his Dallas tenure since arriving in a late-September trade. After making his debut against the Houston Texans, he missed the following game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of a severe intestinal illness. He returned against the Green Bay Packers but was limited by an ankle issue before being ruled inactive for the Week 9 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Porter wants to be available and show the Cowboys what he can contribute, but his injury has kept him from consistently getting on the field. There is at least some positive news regarding his recovery. Porter did not practice Wednesday, but he has started running again after being unable to do so over the previous couple of weeks. Porter's limited availability has also fueled speculation online that his absence could be connected to his contract situation. However, the cornerback dismissed that narrative and made it clear that his priority is returning to the field. "And that's what I'm trying to do: try to get better every day to be out there with the guys again." Dallas will have to wait for the final practice reports before knowing whether Porter can return against San Francisco. His progress is encouraging, but the Cowboys will need to be confident that he is healthy enough to handle the workload before putting him back on the field. If he remains unavailable, Von Miller and Marist Liufau could see more playing time. However, he suffered another concussion in that game. As a result, he has been ruled out of the Week 10 game against the 49ers and could miss several more games. Mingo hurt his ankle in the win over the Colts. He tried to keep playing but couldn’t return, and he missed Wednesday’s practice as he recovers. Before the Nov. 8 game against the Colts, he was dealing with both hamstring and back problems and couldn’t play. He returned to practice on Wednesday, Nov. 11, but was limited because of his hamstring. His return to practice is a positive sign, but it’s still unclear whether he’ll be ready for the 49ers. home.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? The Dallas Cowboys could be getting an important piece of their secondary back at the right time. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is making progress in his recovery from an ankle injury, giving the team some hope that he could return for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. Porter has dealt with an interrupted start to his Dallas tenure since arriving in a late-September trade. After making his debut against the Houston Texans, he missed the following game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of a severe intestinal illness. He returned against the Green Bay Packers but was limited by an ankle issue before being ruled inactive for the Week 9 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Porter wants to be available and show the Cowboys what he can contribute, but his injury has kept him from consistently getting on the field. There is at least some positive news regarding his recovery. Porter did not practice Wednesday, but he has started running again after being unable to do so over the previous couple of weeks. Porter's limited availability has also fueled speculation online that his absence could be connected to his contract situation. However, the cornerback dismissed that narrative and made it clear that his priority is returning to the field. "And that's what I'm trying to do: try to get better every day to be out there with the guys again." Dallas will have to wait for the final practice reports before knowing whether Porter can return against San Francisco. His progress is encouraging, but the Cowboys will need to be confident that he is healthy enough to handle the workload before putting him back on the field. In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

Pittsburgh's momentum will be put to the test in a tough road environment this Sunday night with the AFC North lead on the line. The Steelers have won the turnover battle in three consecutive games. That will be an important factor for them to defeat the Bengals. Burrow has taken good care of the ball this year but did have a three-interception performance just two weeks ago. If the Steelers' defense can force a turnover or two and give their offense support with shorter fields, that will go a long way in helping them keep pace. It's official: Poch to Man United Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steelers vs. Bengals bold predictions for Week 10 Sunday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:19 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The AFC North has been overshadowed by the NFC North to this point in the season, however this division is formidable and clearly the best in the AFC. There's probably just a small difference between this division and their NFC equivalents. The Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals are at the top of the division with 6-2 record, while the Browns are in third place with a 5-4 mark. The injury-plagued Baltimore Ravens are in fourth with a 4-5 record. The NFC North has three teams with six victories, while the first-place Chicago Bears have seven. The Steelers and Bengals are meeting Sunday night to determine the leader in the division. The Steelers have taken advantage of another memorable season from quarterback Aaron Rodgers . The 42-year-old announced that he would be retiring at the end of the season, and he has come through for head coach Mike McCarthy. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rodgers has completed 175 of 288 passes for 1,871 yards with 13 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. He has always been known for his remarkable accuracy, and while he may no longer be at his peak, he is completing 60.8 percent of his passes. The years have slowed him down a bit when it comes to running out of the pocket, and that's something that Rodgers wants to avoid. The Bengals are surging as they prepare for this game against their division rivals. They have won four straight games after a 2-2 start and they are anxious to establish their explosive offense against the nasty Steelers defense. The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 when the two teams met in Pittsburgh in Week 3. Dynamic QB Joe Burrow will throw for 250-plus yards and 3 TDs Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images There's little doubt that Joe Burrow is among the most gifted quarterback in recent memory. Burrow has been troubled by injuries in recent years, but he is healthy and has been showing off his remarkable skill level through the first half of the season. Burrow has completed a shocking 74.0 percent of his passes. He has connected on 219 of 296 passes for 2,386 yards with 23 TDs and 6 interceptions. He appears to be in the lead when it comes to the race for this season's Most Valuable Player award. Burrow has a remarkable 1-2 punch at the wide receiver position with Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase dominating opposing defensive backs. Higgins has caught 48 passes for 758 yards with 6 TDs, and he uses his speed and big-play ability to light up the scoreboard on a regular basis. Chase may be the best receiver in the NFL, although Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks gives him a solid run for the title. Chase has 53 receptions for 647 yards and 7 TDs. Burrow will always look for Chase when the game is on the line. In addition to Higgin and Chase, tight end Mike Gesicki is an excellent red zone weapon, and he could be dangerous in this game. He has caught 26-252-6 through eight games. Rodgers will throw a pair of TD passes to his tight ends The Steelers don't have the superstars at the wide receiver position that the Bengals possess, but Rodgers has demonstrated that he doesn't need the same kind of big plays that the Bengals regularly produce. Wideout DK Metcalf is leading the Steelers in reception. He has caught 33 of 65 targets for 378 yards with 1 TD. More has been expected from Metcalf, and he needs to play more consistently in the second half of the season. The most productive receivers the Steelers have for red zone activity are tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth. Washington uses his size and strength to catch the ball in the end zone. He has 19 receptions for 254 yards and 3 TDs. Freiermuth has a bit more range than Washington, and he has caught 25-235-4. Running back Jaylen Warren has also demonstrated that he can catch passes out of the backfield in addition to his solid ground attack. Warren has caught 25-294-1, and he is also the team's leading rusher 704 yards, a 5.9 yards per carry average and 2 TDs. T.J. Watt will try to limit Burrow's production with 2.0 sacks If the Steelers are going to hold the Bengals' offensive production in check, it will almost certainly involve a powerful game from outside linebacker T.J. Watt. He leads the Bengals with 7.5 sacks and 9.5 tackles for loss. He also has 3 passes defensed, 1 interception that he returned for a touchdown, 1 forced fumble and 1 fumble recovery. Linebacker Payton Wilson is also a key contributor with a team-leading 69 tackles, 7 tackles for loss, 3 passes defensed, 1 interception and 1 fumble recovery. The Steelers rank 7th in total defense, as they are allowing 305.6 yards per game. They are even better as a scoring defense, ranking 4th and allowing just 18.0 points per game. If the Steelers are going to keep the Bengals in check and prevent Burrow from having a huge game, Watt & Co. will have to come up with a peak effort here. away.blurb: 'Who Let the Dogs Out'? Both Pittman and Harmon are eligible to be activated off IR in time for the Week 10 matchup against the Bengals, but as McCarthy pointed out, it remains to be seen if the two Steelers will be cleared for Sunday. Steelers receive huge injury update on two starters - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL It's official: Poch to Man United Steelers receive huge injury update on two starters Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:06 AM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy provided a huge injury update on two players currently on IR. Speaking to reporters on Monday, McCarthy revealed that although Michael Pittman Jr. and Derrick Harmon's status for the Week 10 game against the Cincinnati Bengals remains uncertain, they are "getting close" to returning to action. Pittman, who spent the first six years of his career with the Indianapolis Colts (2020-2025), was traded to the Steelers in March 2026. He re-aggravated a foot injury during Week 5 practice and was subsequently placed on injured reserve on October 10. Harmon, who was drafted by the Steelers in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, had a solid start to the 2026 season, recording 12 combined tackles, one tackle for loss, 1.5 sacks, and one forced fumble during the first four games of the season. He suffered his foot injury in Week 4 and was placed on injured reserve on October 5. home.blurb: Left guard Dylan Fairchild (pectoral), is the new name to monitor this week. Fairchild injured his pectoral late in last Sunday’s victory over the Atlanta Falcons. It caused him to miss the very last snap of the game. Coach Zac Taylor told reporters Wednesday that they’ll take Fairchild day-to-day. Being limited to start the week off is a positive sign. Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) was also limited. There was a chance he wouldn’t play last Sunday, but he was able to Stay in the field for nearly the entire game. Cincinnati will likely take it easy with him until his ankle is fully healed. Defense end Cedric Johnson is notably not included in the injury report, A great sign that his ankle/foot Injury from last week is no longer a concern. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen had his usual rest day. Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column. Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston. Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore. I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track. Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable. Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards. The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver. In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story. Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do. Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9. There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches. Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance. Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play. This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory. Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? This is one of its best remaining opportunities to avoid that nightmare, and I'm picking the Chargers to take advantage. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between six and 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb, head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Friday. Jackson's health has been a primary storyline surrounding the Ravens throughout the 2026 campaign. First, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain.
